=================== startup
---
name: startup
description: >-
  Start of day, or sitting down at either machine: sync this machine against GitHub,
  then report where the last session left off and wait. Use when Eric says '/startup',
  'good morning', 'starting up', 'where did I leave off', 'what was I working on',
  'picking this back up', or opens a session without naming a task. Do not use for the
  end-of-session sign-off (use closeout).
---

# Startup

The front door for a work session on either machine. This skill owns no logic of its own — it runs `dev-sync`, whose Step 5 loads context back in.

## What to do

Invoke the `dev-sync` skill and run it end to end, Step 0 through Step 5.

Do not reimplement any of it here. If the sync behaviour or the context report needs to change, change `dev-sync/SKILL.md`. One home for the procedure, and this file is an alias so the command matches how Eric actually thinks about it: "sync" is what the machine does, "startup" is what he is doing.

## After the report

`dev-sync` Step 5 ends with a short "picking up" report and a stop. Hold there and wait for Eric to confirm or redirect. Do not begin the next task on your own — `docs/STATUS.md` records where the last session stopped, which is not the same as what he wants to do this morning.

If he names a repo when he invokes this, pass it through so Step 5 reports on that one instead of guessing from the most recent commit.

## Not this

- Not the morning brief. Calendar, email and the shape of the day belong to the `morning` / `morning-briefing` work. This skill answers "where was I", not "what's my day".
- Not a memory loader. Global memory arrives through the SessionStart hook before this runs; do not re-read `USER.md` or `MEMORY.md` by hand.
=================== dev-sync
---
name: dev-sync
description: >-
  Bring this machine into line with GitHub and load back the context that came with it:
  locate DEV automatically, pull config and skills, inventory every project, commit and
  push local work, pull the other machine's work, clone what is missing, report
  conflicts, then read the repo's STATUS and latest handoff and report where the last
  session left off. Use when Eric switches machines, sits down to start work, says 'sync
  DEV', asks whether everything is pushed, or asks where he left off. Do not use when
  Eric says '/startup' or 'good morning' (use startup, which runs this sync) or to
  scaffold a new repo (use new-project).
---

# DEV sync

Eric works on a Mac and a Windows laptop. GitHub (`erash11`, all private) is the transport. This skill makes the current machine match GitHub without losing anything on either side. It is the first thing to run when sitting down at a machine.

## Step 0: find DEV (never depend on cwd)

Eric may run this from anywhere. Detect the machine and go to its DEV root:

- macOS (`uname` = Darwin): `~/DEV`
- Windows (PowerShell, or `$OS` = Windows_NT): `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV`

If that folder does not exist, stop and say so. Do not guess another location. Print the root you chose on the first line of output.

## Step 1: config and skills

These are separate repos and the other machine may have changed them:

1. `~/.claude` (repo `dotclaude`): `git pull`. If `~/.claude/machine.md` is missing, copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md` for this OS. Then sync the mods: `bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` (Windows). The folder is the list; put its one line (`mods: N loaded, N disabled, N invalid`) in the report and name any invalid mod. Then apply the 7-day rule: `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply` (`portfolio_json` in `_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It pauses any project started more than 7 days ago with no receiver and no step 1 done, and prints one line plus each project paused or on the clock; put that in the report.
2. `~/.claude/skills` (repo `claude-skills`): `git pull`, then run `sync-to-codex.sh` (Mac) or `sync-to-codex.ps1` (Windows) so Codex sees the shared skills.
3. `~/.claude/global-memory` (repo `claude-global-memory`): `git pull`. **This is the only thing that carries memory between the two machines.** USER.md, MEMORY.md and the handoffs live here. `daily-backup` pushes this repo nightly, but nothing pulled it at the start of a session until this step existed, so a same-day handoff (worked on the Mac after lunch, picked up on Windows that evening) arrived with stale memory. Pull it before anything else reads it. If the pull brings in commits, say how many and name the newest, so it is visible that memory moved.

If any of the three has local uncommitted changes, commit them first with `<machine> snapshot before sync`, then pull, then push.

4. **Mirror project memory across the two slugs.** Tier A memory is keyed by a slug built from the absolute path, so every project has a Mac folder (`-Users-kristinarash-DEV-X`) and a Windows folder (`C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-X`) under `~/.claude/projects/`. dotclaude carries both to both machines, but each machine auto-loads only its own. Before this step existed, 43 memories written on the Mac never loaded on Windows (found 2026-09-24). After the pulls above, run:

   - Mac: `python3 ~/.claude/skills/dev-sync/mirror_memory.py`
   - Windows: `python $HOME\.claude\skills\dev-sync\mirror_memory.py`

   It copies files one side lacks, lets the newer version win when both have one (frontmatter `modified:`, else last commit), merges `MEMORY.md` indexes line by line, creates the twin folder when a project has memory on only one machine, and never deletes. The older side of any replaced file stays in dotclaude history. Put its summary line in the Step 4 report. If it wrote anything, commit `~/.claude` with `<machine> memory mirror` and push, so the other machine gets the result on its next sync.

   Mirroring is a union: a memory deleted on one machine comes back from the other. To retire a memory for good, delete it from both slug folders in the same commit.

Merge note for `global-memory`: `transcripts/.errors.log` and `MEMORY.md` are both append-heavy and both machines write them. On conflict, keep both sides' content rather than choosing one — these are logs, not settings, and a dropped line is a lost memory.

## Step 2: inventory (always show before changing anything)

Walk `DEV/*`, `DEV/Football/*`, and `DEV/SpecialRequests/*`. Skip `.claude`, `_tools`, `_DRIVE` (a link to the Google Drive primary storage drive, not a project; never init it, never walk into it), `token-dashboard` (someone else's remote), and any folder ending in `_OLD_merged*`. For each folder report one of:

- **repo + erash11 remote**: uncommitted count, unpushed count
- **repo, no remote**: needs `gh repo create`
- **not a repo**: needs init + create (use the `new-project` skill's file set)

Then `gh repo list erash11 --limit 300 --json name` and list repos with no local folder. Skip: `dotclaude` (that is `~/.claude`), `SecondBrain`, `claude-skills`, `claude-memory-compiler`, `DEV`, `DexaProject`.

Eric pre-approves these operations; the inventory is for visibility, not a pause for approval, unless something looks wrong (a repo with hundreds of uncommitted files, a large file about to be added).

**Group the report by activity, not alphabetically.** Run `~/.claude/scripts/dev-activity.sh` (Mac) or `dev-activity.ps1` (Windows), which ranks repos by distinct commit days over 90 days. List the active ones individually and collapse the rest to a count: "118 dormant repos: all clean" is the useful line, not 118 names. About 14 repos are genuinely worked at any time; the rest are archives that happen to live in the same folder.

Rank by **commit days, not recency**. On 2026-09-09 a bulk migration gave 43 repos one commit each, after which every one of them looked active by any recency measure. Days-worked is not fooled by that, because a migration touches a repo once.

Nothing is archived or moved on the strength of this. Sorting is a reporting concern. Moving a dormant repo into an archive folder would break three things at once: `harvest-dev-docs` reads `<dir>/docs/*.md` without recursing, so archived repos would silently drop out of the memsearch index; KeystoneOS `projects.json`, `memory-sources.json`, `memory-index-paths.json` and `discovery-roots.json` hold DEV paths; and Tier A project memory is keyed by a slug derived from the absolute path, so moving a repo orphans its memory. Checked 2026-09-12. Do not revive the archive idea without fixing all three first.

## Step 3: apply, per repo

1. If uncommitted: put any untracked file over 95 MB and any `.env` into `.gitignore`, then `git add -A && git commit -m "<machine> snapshot before sync"`.
2. `git fetch origin` then `git merge --no-edit origin/<branch>`.
3. On conflict: keep this machine's version, save the remote version beside it as `<file>.from-mac` or `<file>.from-windows` (whichever the other machine is), stage both, commit. Never discard either side. `.DS_Store` conflicts: just delete the file.

   Save the remote side by **moving the file, never by redirecting stdout**. A
   redirect re-encodes the bytes; on Windows that silently mangles every
   non-ASCII character (an em-dash becomes `ΓÇö`) and adds a UTF-8 BOM, so the
   saved copy is corrupt and every later diff shows a phantom first-line change.

   - PowerShell: `git checkout --theirs -- <f>; Move-Item <f> <f>.from-mac; git checkout --ours -- <f>`
   - bash: `git checkout --theirs -- <f> && mv <f> <f>.from-mac && git checkout --ours -- <f>`

   Never run `git add -A` while `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists — it stages the
   conflict markers themselves and commits a broken file. Stage only the named
   paths you just resolved.
4. `git push`.
5. Missing locally: `gh repo clone erash11/<name> DEV/<name>`.
6. No remote: `gh repo create erash11/<name> --private --source=. --push`.

Windows note: line-ending noise (`LF will be replaced by CRLF`) is normal. If a merge refuses to start because of phantom modifications, run `git add --renormalize .` and commit before merging.

Stale-lock note: if a commit or push fails with `cannot lock ref 'HEAD'`, check
`pgrep -fl git` (or `Get-Process git`) first. If no git is running and the
`.git/*.lock` file is zero bytes and older than the session, it is stale from an
interrupted run. Move it aside — do not delete it — then retry.

## Step 4: verify and report

Re-walk every repo. Report: DEV root used, config and skills pulled (yes/no), the memory-mirror summary line, repos checked, pulled, cloned, created, and any folder still dirty or unpushed. List every `.from-*` file created so Eric can reconcile them. Finish with one line: clean or not.

## Step 4b: start the project board

The live board (`project-triage/board.py`, PM system design Decision 10) writes `portfolio.json`, so it may only start on a registry that has the other machine's edits. Start it only when project-triage came through Step 3 clean: pulled, no `.git/MERGE_HEAD`, no `portfolio.json.from-*` file. Then run, from the folder holding `portfolio_json`:

- Windows: `python board.py --background`
- Mac: `python3 board.py --background`

It reuses a board already running on this machine or starts one tied to this session, opens the page, and prints `board started at <url>` or `board already running at <url>`; put that line in the report. If project-triage did not come through clean, do not start it; report `board: not started, project-triage pull unresolved` and name the conflict. Eric's `pm` (shell) and `/pm` (Claude Code) run the same command later in the day.

## Step 5: pick up where the other machine left off

Syncing git state is only half the job. The other half is loading the context that came with it, and nothing else does this — the SessionStart hook injects global memory, but project state lives in the repo, and Tier A project memory only crosses machines through the Step 1 mirror. This step is the only place that repo context gets read back in.

Do this for the repo Eric names, or the one he is in. If he has not named one, pick from the ACTIVE list in Step 2, not from all 132: take the active repo with the most recent commit and say which you chose. A dormant repo receiving one migration commit must never win this, which is exactly what picking by recency across everything would do.

1. Read `<repo>/AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md` if there is no AGENTS.md).
2. Read `<repo>/docs/STATUS.md`.
3. Read the newest file in `<repo>/docs/handoffs/`, if the folder exists and its newest file is within about two weeks.
4. If `docs/STATUS.md` does not exist in a repo that has real work in it, say so — that repo is invisible to the other machine and closeout should have created it.

Then report, in six lines or fewer, before doing any work:

```
Picking up: <repo>
Last session: <date>, <mac|windows>
Where things stand: <two lines from STATUS.md Current state>
Blocked on: <open questions, or "nothing">
Next: <top one or two from STATUS.md Next>
```

Stop there and wait for Eric to confirm or redirect. Do not start the next task off the back of STATUS.md on your own — it records where work stopped, not what he wants to do this morning.

## Do not

- Do not `rm` anything. Move to a `_to_delete` or `_OLD_*` folder if something must get out of the way.
- Do not rebase or force-push.
- Do not push DexaProject or any repo whose CLAUDE.md says its data must stay local.
=================== closeout
---
name: closeout
description: >-
  End-of-session sign-off ritual. Sweeps loose ends, commits and pushes what needs it,
  verifies memory capture, writes a cross-harness handoff, and reports "clear to sign
  off" or what's still open. Use when the user says "/closeout", "any loose ends?", "am
  I good to sign off?", "close out for the night", "closing out", "goodnight", "wrap up
  for the day", or asks for a system health check before leaving. Do not use at the
  start of a session (use startup) or for a standalone automation health check (use
  claude-stack-doctor).
---

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# Interview Me

End-of-workday synthesis ritual. The user is a sport-science / performance analyst who writes essays connecting sport science, product strategy, and decision-making. The interview's job is to extract publishable insights, not to record what happened.

## Vault location

Use `vault_root` from the selected platform config.

**Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` — load it if unsure; if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins.

- `Inbox/` — full transcripts (one per day)
- `Notes/` — atomic permanent notes (one idea per file)
- `Drafts/` — essays in progress
- `Archive/` — published
- `Templates/interview-note.md`, `Templates/permanent-note.md`
- `Inbox/status-log/` — daily supervisor fact logs (Part 0). Path key: `vault_status_log`.

---

## Part 0 — Supervisor log (90 seconds, ask first)

**Three questions, asked before the reflection questions.** Facts are easier to recall
than insight when the user is tired, and a hard 90-second opener is what makes the ritual
survivable nightly. Reflection quality does not suffer from coming second; it suffers
from the user never starting.

This part exists because `status-report` — the biweekly email to the user's supervisors —
has a sourcing gap: roughly two thirds of what belongs in that email (equipment arriving,
installs, who onboarded onto what, hallway conversations, follow-ups awaiting a reply)
appears in **no** automated source. Without a nightly log, the report has to reconstruct
two weeks from memory. With one, it mostly writes itself.

Ask all three at once. Accept short answers. Do not probe.

> Quick log first, 90 seconds. Then the usual four.
> 1. Anything arrive, get installed, or change hands today? Who's onboarding onto it?
> 2. Who did you talk to that Kenny or Chris would want to know about? Names and sport.
> 3. Waiting on anyone, or anything about to go sideways?

**Honest zero rule.** If all three are genuinely "nothing", write **no file**. A day with
no operational facts is a real day. Padding this log is worse than skipping it, because
`status-report` trusts these entries verbatim.

### Output — `{vault_status_log}/YYYY-MM-DD.md`

```markdown
---
date: YYYY-MM-DD
sports: [Football, Tennis]      # programs named in the answers; [] if none
---

## Equipment & installs
- Perch cameras installed at Foster. Football onboarding this week.

## People & conversations
- Javi (Tennis) — FirstBeat onboarding, wants a one-pager for his staff.

## Waiting on / risks
- Micah, no reply since 8/17.
```

Use the user's own words. Do not editorialize, rank, or add commentary — `status-report`
does the judgement pass later, and it needs raw facts to judge.

**Append, never overwrite.** If today's file exists (a second debrief, or a correction),
add to the existing sections rather than replacing the file.

**This log never becomes a permanent note.** It is a fact record for one downstream
consumer. Insight goes in `Notes/` via Part 1, which is why the skill's "NOT a journaling
app" rule still holds.

---

## Part 0b — Project block (30 seconds, right after Part 0)

The user works a 2-hour calendar block per slate project each week (rules:
`SecondBrain/Projects/Applied-Performance-Operating-Cadence.md`). This question is the only
thing that records whether a block happened; the Friday weekly report counts it, so skipping
it makes a worked week look empty.

Run `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py slate-check` first to get the active project
names. Then ask once:

> Project block: which slate project did you work on today, what moved, and did you finish a step?

- Each project named → `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py add-update <Project> "[block] <what moved, in the user's words>"`.
  The exact `[block]` prefix is what the weekly report counts.
- A step finished → confirm the step name back, then `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py mark-done <Project> --step N`
  (charter order: 1 plan agreed, 2 first draft, 3 final delivered, 4 in use).
- "None" is a real answer — write nothing.
- Work on something **not** on the slate is not a block. If it was a new idea, offer
  `/project idea` and say it waits for a free slot.
- Match names case-insensitively; ask if two projects match. On `[error]`, show it verbatim
  and carry on with Part 1.

---

## Part 1 — The interview

**Time budget:** 10–15 minutes total including Part 0. If the user wants to keep talking, schedule a follow-up session — don't blow the budget.

**Opening line (verbatim is fine):**
> Now the four. Then I write up anything that earned its place.

### Question 1 — Orientation (filter)
> What did you spend time on today?

Listen for themes. Don't try to capture everything. Look for: a hard decision, a piece of work that consumed a lot of time, anything that felt different from yesterday.

### Question 2 — Signal (insight detection)
> What surprised you, frustrated you, or changed your mind?

This is the gold question. Genuine surprise, frustration, or updated belief = the moments worth writing down. If the answer is "nothing," probe once: *"Nothing at all? Even small recalibrations count."* If still nothing, accept and move on — not every day produces signal.

### Question 3 — Pattern (synthesis)
> Does anything from today connect to what you were thinking about earlier this week or recently?

**Optional aid:** quietly Glob `Notes/*.md` modified in the last 7 days; if you find 2–3 candidates that match today's themes, name them and ask if today's experience updates them.

### Question 4 — Essay seed (publishable insight)
> If you told a peer one thing about today's work, what would it be?

This question converts experience into transferable insight. If the user gives a great one-liner — capture it verbatim as the seed for a permanent note.

## Optional source pull-ins

Offer when the user references them. Don't pull unprompted.

- **Meeting referenced** ("today's call with X", "this morning's standup"):
  → **First, check `Inbox/meetings/` for a local summary** — Glob for files matching the date or participant. If found, read and quote from the local file (free, fast, no API call).
  → If not found locally, ask: *"Want me to pull from Fireflies?"* → invoke the `meeting-sync` skill to sync the latest meetings, then read the local file.
  → Fall back to direct `pp-fireflies` only if `meeting-sync` reports nothing matching.
- **Paper / article referenced:**
  → "Want me to pull the source from Zotero?" → use `pp-zotero-research-library` skill.
- **GPS / Catapult data referenced:**
  → "Want me to pull the underlying metric?" → use `pp-catapult-openfield-connect` skill.

Quote sources in the note's frontmatter `source:` field or the **Evidence / origin** section.

## Output protocol

### Write the supervisor log (unless all three answers were nothing)

`Inbox/status-log/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — see Part 0 for the shape. Write this **first**, before
the transcript, so a session that gets cut short still leaves the report its facts.

### Always write the transcript

`Inbox/YYYY-MM-DD-interview.md` — full Q&A, lightly cleaned. Use the `Templates/interview-note.md` skeleton. Fill in `themes`, `notes_produced`, `pulled_sources` in frontmatter.

### Write 0–3 permanent notes

**Bias toward fewer notes.** A vault full of mediocre notes is worse than one with three great ones. If nothing crossed the bar today, write zero — say so to the user. They will respect this.

A note earns its place if it meets at least one of:
- States a transferable claim (works beyond today's context)
- Updates a previously held view (in which case, also update / link the old note)
- Names a pattern across two or more recent days
- Is a clean essay seed the user could draft from later

Each note goes to `Notes/<concept-title-kebab-case>.md` with the `Templates/permanent-note.md` skeleton filled in:
- `created`: today's date
- `source`: `[[YYYY-MM-DD-interview]]`
- `domain`: pick from `sport-science`, `product`, `decision-making`, `leadership`, `methodology`, `personal`
- `tags`: free-form, but reuse existing tags from other Notes when possible
- Body: claim in 1–2 sentences, why it matters, evidence/origin, connections (use `[[wikilink]]` to related Notes), open questions

### Memory bridge (when warranted)

If the interview surfaces a **durable** fact about the user, their projects, or working style that should persist across Claude sessions:
- Also write a Tier A memory file via the `memory-write` skill (it derives the correct project slug from the current working directory) or update USER.md / project_*.md as appropriate.
- Tell the user explicitly: "Also saved this to memory as <name>."
- Do NOT bridge ephemeral notes. Most permanent notes stay in the vault only.

## What NOT to do

- **Don't pad notes with model commentary.** The user's own words and insights are the value. You are a scribe with editorial judgment, not a co-author.
- **Don't ask follow-up questions beyond the four** unless an answer was genuinely ambiguous and one clarification unlocks a much better note.
- **Don't produce a note "just to have one."** Zero notes is an honest output.
- **Don't break the 10–15 min budget.** Offer a follow-up session if needed.
- **Don't write to `Drafts/` from a daily interview.** Drafts come out of weekly synthesis, not daily capture.
- **Don't pad the supervisor log to make the day look productive.** `status-report` copies these entries into an email to the user's supervisors with light editing. An invented install or an inflated conversation becomes a false claim in front of Chris Ruf and Kenny Boyd. No file is the correct output for a quiet day.
- **Don't turn a Part 0 answer into a permanent note** unless it independently clears the Part 1 bar. Operational facts are not insight.

## Gotchas

- **Part 0 goes first, and that ordering is the whole design.** The ritual lapsed for 49 days in 2026 because reflection is expensive when tired. Three factual questions is a low enough floor to clear on a bad day, and a partial run that captures only the log still has value downstream. Moving Part 0 after the four questions quietly reverts the fix.
- **`status-report` reads this directory verbatim.** It counts logged days against the period ("N of 14 days logged") and surfaces the gap to the user. That visible gap is the intended nudge — do not backfill missing days with guesses to make the count look better.
- **Never hardcode the log path.** It is `vault_status_log` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`. The vault has already moved once (off the iCloud-synced Desktop, 2026-08-14) and every hardcoded path broke.
- **Sports named in the answers must go in the `sports:` frontmatter array.** The status report's sport coverage panel — the reason that report exists, since it documents involvement beyond football and basketball — is assembled from this field. A conversation logged without its sport is credit the user does not get.
- **Append to today's file, never overwrite it.** A second debrief on the same day is common and overwriting silently deletes the first pass.

## Weekly synthesis

Weekly synthesis is NOT this skill's job. If the user says "weekly synthesis", "weekly review", or asks to look across the week, invoke the `weekly-review` skill — it owns the Friday ritual (themes, project status, decisions, stale action items, essay angles). This skill is strictly the daily debrief.

## End-of-session sign-off

Always end with a brief summary:
- Supervisor log: saved to `Inbox/status-log/YYYY-MM-DD.md`, or "nothing to log today"
- Transcript saved: `Inbox/YYYY-MM-DD-interview.md`
- Notes created: list with paths and one-line summaries
- Memory bridge: yes/no, what
- Any open thread to revisit tomorrow

Keep it tight — three to five lines.

Then run the registry drift check, the weekly count of projects that live outside the one list:

```bash

```

(`portfolio_json` is in the platform config.) ```bash

- **Project map:** which named projects/clients show up? For each: did they progress (decision made, work shipped), drift (mentioned but no movement), or stick (blocked, awaiting input)?
- **Decision log:** any decision sentences across all sources
- **Stale action items:** anything > 14d old still open
- **Essay clusters:** linked Notes that form a 2–4 note thread on a single idea
- **Threads worth carrying forward**
- **Unlabeled-speaker meetings:** while reading `Inbox/meetings/*.md`, grep for `Speaker 1`, `Speaker 2`, `Speaker 3` (etc.) patterns. Track which meeting files still have unnamed speakers. PM system design Decision 6: paused projects untouched for 30+ days get a decision, 10 a week, oldest first, so the paused backlog clears instead of growing. Run:

```

- Headline number: N meetings, M interviews, K notes synthesized

- One open question worth them thinking about before next Monday

# Meeting Sync

Pull new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault. Each meeting becomes one markdown file at `Inbox/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD_<title>.md`.

## Paths — shared config

`scripts/sync.py` reads these itself; don't hardcode paths elsewhere. If the vault ever moves, edit the config only.

sync.py passes `--limit 100000` to `transcripts find` — the CLI's default is 100, which silently truncates large backfills. Don't remove that flag.

## Prerequisite — one-time auth

Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` environment variable (see the `pp-fireflies` skill's Auth Setup). Verify with `fireflies-pp-cli doctor --agent` — the JSON must show `"auth": "configured"`. `scripts/sync.py` runs this check itself and exits with code 4 if auth is missing. In that case, stop and tell the user:

> Fireflies isn't authenticated yet. Set `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` in your environment (System Properties → Environment Variables on Windows), then restart your terminal. After that, `/meeting-sync` will work.

Do not try to fix auth yourself (no `auth set-token` — the env var is the canonical mechanism). Then exit.

## Sync flow

### 1. Run the pipeline script

The deterministic pipeline (doctor check → CLI sync → find → state diff → export → state update) is fully implemented in `scripts/sync.py`. Two-phase invocation:

**Phase A — list pending, check titles:**
```bash
python scripts/sync.py --list-only [--days-back N]
```
Prints a JSON array of not-yet-exported transcripts: `[{"id", "title", "date"}]`. Diagnostics go to stderr.

**Phase B — export:**
```bash
python scripts/sync.py --no-sync [--days-back N]
```
Prints a JSON array of newly exported absolute file paths (`--no-sync` skips the redundant DB refresh Phase A just did). Exports are detected by diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export — never "most recent .md" — so a no-op export can't claim an unrelated file.

`[days-back]` argument from the user maps to `--days-back N`; otherwise the config default applies.

### 2. Between phases: generic-title judgment (model's job)

The user does not name their Fireflies meetings consistently. Generic titles produce useless filenames in the vault. Check each pending `title` from Phase A against the generic patterns documented in the `name-meetings` skill (empty, `Zoom Meeting`, `Recording`, `Meeting`, date-only, etc.).

- **0 generics:** run Phase B immediately, silently.
- **1–3 generics:** use `AskUserQuestion` once — question: "N of the new meetings have generic titles. Name them before exporting?" with options **[Propose names first / Export as-is]**. If "Propose names first", invoke the `name-meetings` skill scoped to just these IDs, then re-run Phase A to pick up renamed titles before Phase B.
- **4+ generics:** report the count and suggest: *"Several new meetings have generic titles. Run `/name-meetings` to clean them up — I'll proceed with the export either way."* Then run Phase B without blocking.

This keeps the rename loop tight at sync-time without blocking the pipeline.

### 3. Augment each exported file (model's job)

For each path in Phase B's JSON output, the file is raw Fireflies markdown. Insert the fixed 5-section header from `assets/meeting-header.md` (this skill's folder) at the top — after frontmatter, before any existing content. Read the asset and prepend it verbatim.

Leave the Fireflies-generated transcript and summary below this block intact. This gives the user **5 fixed sections to fill in or curate** during interview-me / weekly-review, on top of the raw Fireflies content.

### 4. Tag each exported file with its project (script's job)

After the header is in place, pass the same paths to the tagger:

```bash
python scripts/tag_project.py <path> [<path> ...]
```

It asks TypeSafe's Jev which `portfolio.json` project each meeting is mainly about, and adds `- project/<PortfolioName>` under `## Project tags` only when the answer is confident. It always adds one `<!-- jev-project: ... -->` line recording what was asked and answered, which is also how a rerun knows to skip the note. `meeting-prep` reads the `- project/` line to find a project's meetings.

It never blocks the sync: no key, no network or no transcript just leaves the note untagged and logs to stderr. Relay any `WARNING` lines. Run it only after step 3, because notes without a `## Project tags` header are skipped.

## Drift audit (periodic, not every sync)

A vault filename is a snapshot of the Fireflies title at export time. Titles get renamed afterwards, so the two drift apart. `scripts/audit_filenames.py` detects this by asking the export CLI to regenerate every filename into a scratch dir and diffing against the ledger — **the slug algorithm is never reimplemented**, the CLI is the authority.

```bash
python scripts/audit_filenames.py [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--skip-linkcheck] [--report PATH]
```

Run it from `weekly-review`, or on demand — **not** on every sync (it spawns one CLI call per ledger entry, ~2-4 min for a full vault). Same exit codes as sync.py; drift itself is not an error, read the counts in the JSON.

It classifies every mismatch, and the classes need different responses:

- **`regression`** — the vault name is good and Fireflies has reverted to an auto-generated stamp (`Jan_19_0445_PM`, `Untitled`, `Audio_Message`). **Never re-export these — it destroys the good name.** Fix the title upstream in Fireflies instead. Note the API refuses title updates on some older meetings; if so, say so and leave the vault alone (the ledger already protects it).
- **`semantic`** — the title genuinely differs in meaning. Usually two generations of AI naming rather than rot, so it needs a human call, not an automatic rename. Surface it, don't act.
- **`cosmetic`** — same words, different separators (`RTP_UpperExtremity` vs `RTP___Upper_Extremity`). Ignore; re-exporting is pure churn.

Before proposing any rename, check `inbound_links` in the output. Renaming a vault file breaks `[[wikilinks]]` from weekly-review notes and `GRAPH_REPORT.md`. Rewrite those links in the same pass or leave the file alone.

## Output to user

When done, report:
- N transcripts found in the window (stderr line from sync.py)
- M new exports written, K tagged with a project
- Path: `Inbox/meetings/`
- If 0 new: just say "No new meetings since last sync."

Keep it to 3 lines.

## Error handling

sync.py exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/config, 3 sync/find failure, 4 auth not configured.

- **Exit 4 (auth):** deliver the auth message from Prerequisite above, stop.
- **Exit 3 (sync/find):** report the stderr error verbatim, do not try to recover. The user may need to refresh their API key.
- **Export fails for one transcript:** sync.py logs a warning to stderr and continues with the rest; relay which one failed.
- **State file corrupted:** sync.py backs it up to `.sync-state.json.bak` and recreates fresh automatically (re-export is idempotent on the filesystem because filenames are deterministic per CLI); flag this in the report if the warning appears.

## Gotchas

- **Two tag vocabularies share `## Project tags`.** Hand tags are topic words (`project/rtp`, `project/load-monitoring`). Jev tags are exact `portfolio.json` names (`project/Sport_Tech_Vetting`). The tagger only appends and never edits or removes a hand tag.
- **Measured before shipping, so don't tune the question here.** The question wording and the 0.60 threshold in `tag_project.py` were tested blind on 40 meetings (TypeSafe_Sandbox `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md`, 2026-09-22). Jev was confident on 36, and right on 33 of those. It never confidently tagged a non-project meeting, but it found only 7 of 11 real project meetings. OKRs_2026-27 was the repeat miss. Judge any wording change against meetings the test didn't use.
- **A missing tag is not evidence the meeting is unrelated.** The marker line says `none of these` or `(unsure)`. Callers still fall back to text search.
- **Probabilities wobble by a few points between runs** (for example 0.83 vs 0.81 on the same note). Notes near 0.60 can go either way, which is one reason the marker is written once and not re-asked.
- **Vault notes can mix CRLF and LF lines.** The tagger splices in its lines and never re-encodes the file. Don't "clean up" line endings in this script: an earlier draft did, and rewrote about 50 lines of one note.

## What NOT to do

- **Don't re-implement steps the script owns** — doctor, CLI sync, find, state diff, export, state update all live in `scripts/sync.py`.
- **Don't identify exports by "newest .md file"** — that's the exact bug the directory-diff in sync.py fixes.
- **Don't detect filename drift by pattern-matching for "generic-looking" names** — that both misses real drift and invents fake drift. Use `audit_filenames.py`, which compares against what the export CLI actually produces.
- **Don't bulk re-export to "clean up" filenames.** Most mismatches are cosmetic or a second valid naming generation, and the `regression` class gets actively worse. Re-export only what a human approved.
- **Don't modify the Fireflies-generated content** of the exported file — only PREPEND the header from `assets/meeting-header.md`. The transcript and AI summary stay untouched.
- **Don't sync every interaction.** Run sync only when explicitly invoked OR when called by weekly-review / fireflies-intake.

# Meeting Prep

Answers one question before the user walks into a room: **"Is everything I said I'd do actually reflected in the artifacts, and what do I need to raise?"**

The argument (or conversation context) names the project — e.g. FaceComps, RTP presentation, AppPerformance brief. If no project is named and none is obvious from context, ask which meeting this is for; that is the only question to ask.

## Step 1 — Reconstruct the "last agreed state"

Pull the most recent decisions about this project, cheapest source first:

1. Project memory files (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`) and global `MEMORY.md` active threads.
2. The most recent SecondBrain meeting note(s) for the project. First grep the meeting notes for the line `- project/<PortfolioName>`, matching the name case-insensitively (written by `meeting-sync` step 4). Then also search for notes that mention the project, because untagged meetings are common: only about 2 in 3 project meetings get a tag. (the meeting-sync output in the vault — **Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`, e.g. `vault_inbox_meetings`; load it if unsure — if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins).
3. If still thin, `memsearch search "<project> decision" --top-k 5`.

Produce a short internal list: what was decided, what was promised, by when.

## Step 2 — Verify the artifacts match

For each decided/promised item, check the actual artifact — not the conversation:

- Open the current deliverable files (deck, PDF, calendar, spreadsheet, app) and confirm the agreed change is present.
- `git log --since="<last meeting date>"` in the project repo to see what actually shipped.
- Note any artifact that is stale, locked, or missing.

Mark each item ✅ implemented / ⚠️ partially / ❌ not reflected.

## Step 3 — The brief

Output one screen, in this order:

```
## Meeting Prep — <project> (<meeting date/person if known>)

**Bottom line:** ready / ready with caveats / gaps found

**Since last meeting:** <2-4 bullets of what changed/shipped>

**Decision check:**
✅ <decision> — in <file path>
❌ <decision> — NOT reflected; <where it should be>

**Bring up in the meeting:** <open questions, items awaiting their input>

**Deliverables & paths:** <every file they might present or reference, full paths>
```

## Rules

- Verify against files, never against memory of the conversation — the whole point is catching drift between "we decided" and "it's in the deck."
- If a gap is small and mechanical (a label, a date), offer to fix it now in one line — don't just report it.
- Do not restructure or "improve" deliverables uninvited; this is a readiness check, not an editing pass.
- Brevity is the deliverable: the user is reading this minutes before a meeting.

151	
152	# Meeting Sync
153	
154	Pull new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault. Each meeting becomes one markdown file at `Inbox/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD_<title>.md`.
155	
156	## Paths — shared config
157	
158	Vault and state-file paths live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` (single source of truth):
159	- `vault_inbox_meetings` — platform-specific export target
160	- `meeting_sync_state_file` — idempotency ledger (`.sync-state.json` in that folder)
161	- `meeting_lookback_days` — default window (14)
162	
163	`scripts/sync.py` reads these itself; don't hardcode paths elsewhere. If the vault ever moves, edit the config only.
164	
165	sync.py passes `--limit 100000` to `transcripts find` — the CLI's default is 100, which silently truncates large backfills. Don't remove that flag.
166	
167	## Prerequisite — one-time auth
168	
169	Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` environment variable (see the `pp-fireflies` skill's Auth Setup). Verify with `fireflies-pp-cli doctor --agent` — the JSON must show `"auth": "configured"`. `scripts/sync.py` runs this check itself and exits with code 4 if auth is missing. In that case, stop and tell the user:
170	
171	> Fireflies isn't authenticated yet. Set `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` in your environment (System Properties → Environment Variables on Windows), then restart your terminal. After that, `/meeting-sync` will work.
172	
173	Do not try to fix auth yourself (no `auth set-token` — the env var is the canonical mechanism). Then exit.
174	
175	## Sync flow
176	
177	### 1. Run the pipeline script
178	
179	The deterministic pipeline (doctor check → CLI sync → find → state diff → export → state update) is fully implemented in `scripts/sync.py`. Two-phase invocation:
180	
181	**Phase A — list pending, check titles:**
182	```bash
183	python scripts/sync.py --list-only [--days-back N]
184	```
185	Prints a JSON array of not-yet-exported transcripts: `[{"id", "title", "date"}]`. Diagnostics go to stderr.
186	
187	**Phase B — export:**
188	```bash
189	python scripts/sync.py --no-sync [--days-back N]
190	```
191	Prints a JSON array of newly exported absolute file paths (`--no-sync` skips the redundant DB refresh Phase A just did). Exports are detected by diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export — never "most recent .md" — so a no-op export can't claim an unrelated file.
192	
193	`[days-back]` argument from the user maps to `--days-back N`; otherwise the config default applies.
194	
195	### 2. Between phases: generic-title judgment (model's job)
196	
197	The user does not name their Fireflies meetings consistently. Generic titles produce useless filenames in the vault. Check each pending `title` from Phase A against the generic patterns documented in the `name-meetings` skill (empty, `Zoom Meeting`, `Recording`, `Meeting`, date-only, etc.).
198	
199	- **0 generics:** run Phase B immediately, silently.
200	- **1–3 generics:** use `AskUserQuestion` once — question: "N of the new meetings have generic titles. Name them before exporting?" with options **[Propose names first / Export as-is]**. If "Propose names first", invoke the `name-meetings` skill scoped to just these IDs, then re-run Phase A to pick up renamed titles before Phase B.
201	- **4+ generics:** report the count and suggest: *"Several new meetings have generic titles. Run `/name-meetings` to clean them up — I'll proceed with the export either way."* Then run Phase B without blocking.
202	
203	This keeps the rename loop tight at sync-time without blocking the pipeline.
204	
205	### 3. Augment each exported file (model's job)
206	
207	For each path in Phase B's JSON output, the file is raw Fireflies markdown. Insert the fixed 5-section header from `assets/meeting-header.md` (this skill's folder) at the top — after frontmatter, before any existing content. Read the asset and prepend it verbatim.
208	
209	Leave the Fireflies-generated transcript and summary below this block intact. This gives the user **5 fixed sections to fill in or curate** during interview-me / weekly-review, on top of the raw Fireflies content.
210	
211	### 4. Tag each exported file with its project (script's job)
212	
213	After the header is in place, pass the same paths to the tagger:
214	
215	```bash
216	python scripts/tag_project.py <path> [<path> ...]
217	```
218	
219	It asks TypeSafe's Jev which `portfolio.json` project each meeting is mainly about, and adds `- project/<PortfolioName>` under `## Project tags` only when the answer is confident. It always adds one `<!-- jev-project: ... -->` line recording what was asked and answered, which is also how a rerun knows to skip the note. `meeting-prep` reads the `- project/` line to find a project's meetings.
220	
221	It never blocks the sync: no key, no network or no transcript just leaves the note untagged and logs to stderr. Relay any `WARNING` lines. Run it only after step 3, because notes without a `## Project tags` header are skipped.
222	
223	## Drift audit (periodic, not every sync)
224	
225	A vault filename is a snapshot of the Fireflies title at export time. Titles get renamed afterwards, so the two drift apart. `scripts/audit_filenames.py` detects this by asking the export CLI to regenerate every filename into a scratch dir and diffing against the ledger — **the slug algorithm is never reimplemented**, the CLI is the authority.
226	
227	```bash
228	python scripts/audit_filenames.py [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--skip-linkcheck] [--report PATH]
229	```
230	
231	Run it from `weekly-review`, or on demand — **not** on every sync (it spawns one CLI call per ledger entry, ~2-4 min for a full vault). Same exit codes as sync.py; drift itself is not an error, read the counts in the JSON.
232	
233	It classifies every mismatch, and the classes need different responses:
234	
235	- **`regression`** — the vault name is good and Fireflies has reverted to an auto-generated stamp (`Jan_19_0445_PM`, `Untitled`, `Audio_Message`). **Never re-export these — it destroys the good name.** Fix the title upstream in Fireflies instead. Note the API refuses title updates on some older meetings; if so, say so and leave the vault alone (the ledger already protects it).
236	- **`semantic`** — the title genuinely differs in meaning. Usually two generations of AI naming rather than rot, so it needs a human call, not an automatic rename. Surface it, don't act.
237	- **`cosmetic`** — same words, different separators (`RTP_UpperExtremity` vs `RTP___Upper_Extremity`). Ignore; re-exporting is pure churn.
238	
239	Before proposing any rename, check `inbound_links` in the output. Renaming a vault file breaks `[[wikilinks]]` from weekly-review notes and `GRAPH_REPORT.md`. Rewrite those links in the same pass or leave the file alone.
240	
241	## Output to user
242	
243	When done, report:
244	- N transcripts found in the window (stderr line from sync.py)
245	- M new exports written, K tagged with a project
246	- Path: `Inbox/meetings/`
247	- If 0 new: just say "No new meetings since last sync."
248	
249	Keep it to 3 lines.
250	
251	## Error handling
252	
253	sync.py exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/config, 3 sync/find failure, 4 auth not configured.
254	
255	- **Exit 4 (auth):** deliver the auth message from Prerequisite above, stop.
256	- **Exit 3 (sync/find):** report the stderr error verbatim, do not try to recover. The user may need to refresh their API key.
257	- **Export fails for one transcript:** sync.py logs a warning to stderr and continues with the rest; relay which one failed.
258	- **State file corrupted:** sync.py backs it up to `.sync-state.json.bak` and recreates fresh automatically (re-export is idempotent on the filesystem because filenames are deterministic per CLI); flag this in the report if the warning appears.
259	
260	## Gotchas
261	
262	- **Two tag vocabularies share `## Project tags`.** Hand tags are topic words (`project/rtp`, `project/load-monitoring`). Jev tags are exact `portfolio.json` names (`project/Sport_Tech_Vetting`). The tagger only appends and never edits or removes a hand tag.
263	- **Measured before shipping, so don't tune the question here.** The question wording and the 0.60 threshold in `tag_project.py` were tested blind on 40 meetings (TypeSafe_Sandbox `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md`, 2026-09-22). Jev was confident on 36, and right on 33 of those. It never confidently tagged a non-project meeting, but it found only 7 of 11 real project meetings. OKRs_2026-27 was the repeat miss. Judge any wording change against meetings the test didn't use.
264	- **A missing tag is not evidence the meeting is unrelated.** The marker line says `none of these` or `(unsure)`. Callers still fall back to text search.
265	- **Probabilities wobble by a few points between runs** (for example 0.83 vs 0.81 on the same note). Notes near 0.60 can go either way, which is one reason the marker is written once and not re-asked.
266	- **Vault notes can mix CRLF and LF lines.** The tagger splices in its lines and never re-encodes the file. Don't "clean up" line endings in this script: an earlier draft did, and rewrote about 50 lines of one note.
267	
268	## What NOT to do
269	
270	- **Don't re-implement steps the script owns** — doctor, CLI sync, find, state diff, export, state update all live in `scripts/sync.py`.
271	- **Don't identify exports by "newest .md file"** — that's the exact bug the directory-diff in sync.py fixes.
272	- **Don't detect filename drift by pattern-matching for "generic-looking" names** — that both misses real drift and invents fake drift. Use `audit_filenames.py`, which compares against what the export CLI actually produces.
273	- **Don't bulk re-export to "clean up" filenames.** Most mismatches are cosmetic or a second valid naming generation, and the `regression` class gets actively worse. Re-export only what a human approved.
274	- **Don't modify the Fireflies-generated content** of the exported file — only PREPEND the header from `assets/meeting-header.md`. The transcript and AI summary stay untouched.
275	- **Don't sync every interaction.** Run sync only when explicitly invoked OR when called by weekly-review / fireflies-intake.

296	
297	Pull the most recent decisions about this project, cheapest source first:
298

300	2. The most recent SecondBrain meeting note(s) for the project. First grep the meeting notes for the line `- project/<PortfolioName>`, matching the name case-insensitively (written by `meeting-sync` step 4). Then also search for notes that mention the project, because untagged meetings are common: only about 2 in 3 project meetings get a tag. (the meeting-sync output in the vault — **Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`, e.g. `vault_inbox_meetings`; load it if unsure — if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins).

311	- Note any artifact that is stale, locked, or missing.

331

407	# Name Meetings
408	
409	The user does not name their Fireflies meetings. Without names, exported filenames are useless for retrieval (`2026-05-20_meeting.md`). This skill proposes structured titles from existing AI summaries and applies them via `scripts/rename.py`, which writes back to Fireflies as source-of-truth and verifies each write by read-back.
410	
411	Detail lives in [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md) — load the section you need, not the whole file.
412	
413	## Prerequisite
414	
415	Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` env var (see `pp-fireflies` → Auth Setup; do not use `auth set-token`). Verify:
416	
417	```bash
418	fireflies-pp-cli doctor --agent
419	```
420	
421	If the JSON does not show `"auth": "configured"`, halt and tell the user:
422	> Fireflies isn't authenticated. Set `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` in your environment (System Properties → Environment Variables on Windows), then restart your terminal.
423	
424	## Resume mode — check this FIRST
425	
426	Before anything else, check the pending-renames file (`pending_renames_file` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). If `pending[]` has entries, tell the user you're resuming and apply them; if only `review[]` has entries, run them through the approval flow. Full loop: [REFERENCE.md → Resume mode](REFERENCE.md#resume-mode--full-loop).
427	
428	Only proceed to the flow below if the file is absent or both arrays are empty.
429	
430	## Flow
431	
432	### 1. Refresh and list candidates
433	
434	```bash
435	fireflies-pp-cli sync --full --resources transcripts --agent
436	fireflies-pp-cli transcripts find --from 30 --processed-only --limit 100000 --json --agent
437	```
438	
439	`--full` is required: an incremental sync leaves the DB stale and `find` then under-reports candidates. `--limit 100000` overrides the CLI default of 100. See [REFERENCE.md → CLI gotchas](REFERENCE.md#cli-gotchas).
440	
441	Default lookback is 30 days. Adjust `--from` if the user says "last 60 days" / "all meetings" (omitting it means all-time — warn that high-volume rename is slow).
442	
443	### 2. Detect generics, then check they're editable
444	
445	Match each title against the patterns in [REFERENCE.md → Generic-title patterns](REFERENCE.md#generic-title-patterns). Skip everything else — **don't rename what the user has already curated.** A date *prefix* followed by content (`2026-01-30_BAIR_Steering_Approval`) is curated; only date-and-time-*only* titles are generic.
446	
447	**Expect ghosts.** `sync --full` doesn't prune transcripts deleted from the Fireflies cloud, so `find` can list meetings that no longer exist. They fail at step 5 with `Transcript not found` — literally true, and permanent. Reads don't detect them (`transcripts get` returns full data for a deleted transcript on both `live` and `local`), so you can't pre-filter; the write is the only reliable signal. Don't skip candidates by age — see [REFERENCE.md → Deleted transcripts](REFERENCE.md#deleted-transcripts-linger-in-the-local-db).
448	
449	### 3. Propose titles
450	
451	For each candidate, pull the content before proposing anything:
452	
453	```bash
454	fireflies-pp-cli summary <id> --format gist --json --agent
455	```
456	
457	The gist, keywords, overview, and the speaker names in `action_items` are enough to build a title. Follow [REFERENCE.md → Title construction rules](REFERENCE.md#title-construction-rules). If the gist is too vague, propose `[skip — gist too vague]` and tell the user it needs manual naming in the Fireflies UI.
458	
459	If several candidates come from one event, offer a shared prefix so they group — ask what the event was rather than guessing.
460	
461	### 4. Present batch for approval
462	
463	Display a markdown table with columns `# | Date | Current | Proposed | Action` (`✓` to apply, `—` to skip). Then `AskUserQuestion`: "How should I apply these renames?" with **[Approve all / Edit rows / Apply subset / Cancel]**:
464	
465	- **Approve all** → apply all non-skipped rows
466	- **Edit rows** → ask which rows and what titles, confirm the revised table, then apply
467	- **Apply subset** → ask which rows ("1,3,5" / "rows 1-2" / "skip 2,4"), apply only those
468	- **Cancel** → exit without applying
469	
470	### 5. Apply approved renames
471	
472	```bash
473	python3 ~/.claude/skills/name-meetings/scripts/rename.py <id> "<new title>"
474	```
475	
476	**Never use `fireflies-pp-cli transcripts update`, and never use the Fireflies MCP tool `fireflies_update_meeting_title`.** Both are broken, and the MCP one lies — it returns `success: true` without reliably writing. `scripts/rename.py` calls the API directly and **verifies every write by reading the title back**, so it cannot report a silent failure as a success. Full diagnosis: [REFERENCE.md → Why renames bypass the CLI and MCP](REFERENCE.md#why-renames-bypass-the-cli-and-mcp).
477	
478	The script spaces its own writes and verifies each one. Run it once per meeting, or `python3 ~/.claude/skills/name-meetings/scripts/rename.py --pending` to apply a whole approved batch and prune the ledger as each one verifies. Trust its `OK` / `FAIL` lines — never a bare success flag. On a 429, stop and persist the rest to `pending[]`.
479	
480	**Classify every other failure before queuing it — the ledger is for transient errors only.**
481	- *Transient* (timeout, blocked call, 5xx, connection reset) → retry once, then append to `pending[]`
482	- *Permanent* (`Transcript not found`, or a title under 5 / over 256 characters) → **do not queue.** Resume mode auto-applies `pending[]`, so a permanent failure there retries forever and can never succeed. Report it as unrenamable, with the reason.
483	- A `read-back mismatch` from `rename.py` is **transient** — the write did not land. Retry once, then queue it.
484	
485	Report each result inline. Mechanics and fallbacks: [REFERENCE.md → Rate limits and the retry ledger](REFERENCE.md#rate-limits-and-the-retry-ledger).
486	
487	### 6. Re-sync — must be `--full`
488	
489	```bash
490	fireflies-pp-cli sync --full --resources transcripts --agent
491	```
492	
493	**Plain `sync --agent` fails silently here** — it skips already-seen transcripts, so title edits never land, and it still exits 0 reporting `total: 0`. **Verify by re-running the step-1 `find` and confirming the new titles**, not by reading the exit code.
494	
495	If the verification `find` surfaces generics you never proposed, the earlier DB was stale — say so and offer to name them rather than ending the run silently.
496	
497	**Fireflies' list endpoint lags its single-transcript endpoint by minutes.** `sync` and `find` read the list; `rename.py` verifies against the single transcript. So immediately after a rename it is normal and expected for `find` to still show the old title while the rename is genuinely applied. Do **not** re-issue the rename — that is how a good title gets clobbered. Wait ~4 minutes, re-run `sync --full`, and check again. This matters most when `meeting-sync` runs next: it builds vault filenames from the synced title, so exporting too early bakes the stale title into the filename, and a later re-export creates a *second* file rather than fixing the first.
498	
499	**If the sync fails**, retry once. If it fails again the renames are NOT lost — Fireflies is source-of-truth and they already succeeded there; only the local DB is stale. Report explicitly: *"Renames applied in Fireflies, but the local DB re-sync failed — titles will look stale to meeting-sync/weekly-review until you run `fireflies-pp-cli sync --full --resources transcripts --agent`."* Never end with a silent DB/Fireflies mismatch.
500	
501	### 7. Report
502	
503	3–5 lines: N scanned / M generic · K applied · F queued in `.pending-renames.json` (next run auto-resumes) · S skipped for manual naming · re-sync status (OK, or the stale-DB warning).
504	
505	## When invoked by `meeting-sync`
506	
507	- Detect generics only in the **new-since-last-sync** subset (the IDs meeting-sync passes), not the full 30-day window
508	- If 0 generics: return silently
509	- meeting-sync has already asked the user, so go straight to proposing, then the normal approval flow
510	
511	## Unattended mode
512	
513	Only when an orchestrating skill explicitly declares it (`fireflies-intake` does): apply HIGH-confidence renames without approval, queue everything else to `review[]`. Rules: [REFERENCE.md → Unattended mode](REFERENCE.md#unattended-mode). This is the only sanctioned exception to the approval rule.
514	
515	## What NOT to do
516	
517	- **Don't rename meetings the user already titled.** Curated titles are sacred.
518	- **Don't propose without seeing the gist.** Without content you'll guess wrong; if `summary` fails, mark as skip.
519	- **Don't auto-apply without approval** — except Unattended mode, and there only HIGH-confidence.
520	- **Don't trust a sync's exit code.** Verify with `find`.
521	- **Don't include the date in the title.** Filenames already prefix dates.
522	- **Don't pad titles to meet length.** Concise > complete.
523	- **Don't rename in bulk if Fireflies rate-limits** — back off and report applied vs pending.
524	=================== decision-audit
525	---
526	name: decision-audit
527	description: "Decision Drain Audit: sort the decisions Eric has been avoiding into four buckets (decide now, needs one piece of information, waiting on someone, not mine), name why they are stuck, give 3 tiny next actions, then optionally decide them and record each answer where it lives. Use when the user says \"/decision-audit\", \"decision drain audit\", \"what decisions am I avoiding\", \"what's stuck\", \"fill out my pending decisions\", or \"let's work through the decisions\". Do not use for the Friday synthesis (use weekly-review), ranking projects (use project), or the biweekly report (use status-report)."
528	---
529	
530	# Decision Audit
531	
532	Turns a vague sense of "too many open loops" into a sorted list, a short plan, and
533	decisions recorded in the repos. First run: 2026-10-02 (`runs.md`).
534	
535	Files in this folder:
536	- `checklist.md` — the run checklist. Tick it as you go.
537	- `templates/audit-report.md` — the exact output shape for Steps 2-4.
538	- `references/mining-prompt.md` — the subagent prompt for Step 1 (mine mode).
539	- `runs.md` — one line per run. Append at the end of every run.
540	
541	## Step 1 — Get the list (8-20 items, one line each)
542	
543	Two modes. Ask which only if the user hasn't said.
544	
545	- **Ask mode:** ask for 8-20 pending decisions, big or small, work or personal, one
546	  line each. Offer 3-4 seeds from `## Pending Decisions` and `## Active Threads` in the
547	  injected Tier B `MEMORY.md`.
548	- **Mine mode** ("go through our recent work"): spawn ONE general-purpose subagent with
549	  `references/mining-prompt.md` (fill in the window, default 30 days). Keep only its
550	  findings in context.
551	
552	Then **stale-check before sorting.** On 2026-10-02, 4 of 22 mined items were already
553	settled (a merged PR, an ownership call made two weeks earlier, a format shipped by a PR,
554	a promotion done that morning). For each candidate, grep the latest `docs/STATUS.md` and
555	`gh pr view` where a PR is named. Drop or mark settled ones; say so in one line.
556	
557	Keep choices, drop chores. "Rotate the credential" is a chore; "rotate now or accept the
558	risk" is a choice. Never read `DexaProject`, never quote ContextVault detail.
559	
560	## Step 2 — Sort into exactly four buckets, then name 1-2 hidden reasons
561	
562	Use `templates/audit-report.md`. Bucket rules:
563	
564	| Bucket | Goes here when |
565	|---|---|
566	| Ready to Decide Now | Eric already has everything; only the choice is missing. Default bucket when unsure. |
567	| Needs One Piece of Information | Exactly one named fact, check, or answer unblocks it. Name the piece. |
568	| Waiting on Someone Else | A named person must act first. Name them. If Eric owes a nudge, say so. |
569	| Not Actually Mine to Decide | Someone else owns the choice (funding, membership, another unit's policy). Name Eric's sliver, e.g. "you own the recommendation and which dataset is authoritative". |
570	
571	Hidden reasons: 1-2, drawn from the pattern in *this* list, stated plainly ("sharpened,
572	not soothed"). Patterns seen before (check these first, don't force them):
573	- **Built but not shipped.** The last step needs another person to see it (post, send,
574	  merge, walkthrough). Building feels like progress; exposure doesn't.
575	- **Options with no default.** "X or Y?" with no recommended answer and no date, so every
576	  option stays live and the same question resurfaces.
577	- **One root, many items.** Several entries are the same undecided direction (2026-10-02:
578	  four TypeSafe/Jev items were one "maintenance or keep hunting" call).
579	
580	## Step 3 — Next 60 Minutes + mantra
581	
582	Exactly 3 actions, each under 10 minutes, each with a time estimate and a concrete
583	artifact (a call booked, a line in a named STATUS file, a one-question message with a
584	reply-by date). Pick the most *draining* items, not the easiest: oldest, personal, or
585	most-recurring first. Close with one calm one-sentence mantra.
586	
587	## Step 4 — Decide in rounds (when the user says "let's work through them")
588	
589	1. Pull context for each Ready item first (grep its STATUS, open questions, memory) so
590	   every option is grounded. Re-run the stale check here; it catches more.
591	2. `AskUserQuestion`, max 4 questions per call, recommended option first with
592	   "(Recommended)", one-line trade-off per option. Use `multiSelect` for batch
593	   keep/archive calls.
594	3. Restate the answers in one line after each round.
595	
596	## Step 5 — Record every decision where it lives
597	
598	A decision only counts once it is written where the next session will look:
599	
600	| Decision type | Where |
601	|---|---|
602	| Project question | That repo's `docs/STATUS.md`: rewrite the open question as `ANSWERED YYYY-MM-DD: <question>? <answer>.`; if none, a dated bullet at the top of Current state. |
603	| Project status (done, parked, paused) | `project-triage/portfolio.json` via `python portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>"`; status changes via `portfolio.load_registry`/`save_registry` (no CLI verb). Separate commit, subject `data: ...`. |
604	| Cross-project pending decision | Tier B `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions` (remove when closed; cap 2,500 chars). |
605	| Personal / durable user fact | Tier A file via the `memory-write` skill. |
606	| Method or content position | The doc itself (e.g. Flint `docs/method-baseline.md` tension marked RESOLVED). |
607	
608	Batch the repo writes to one general-purpose subagent with an explicit per-repo list.
609	It commits only the files it changed, never force-pushes, never moves folders. Archive
610	means *recorded*, not moved, unless the user says move. **Ask before the first commit
611	and push** unless the user already said go this session.
612	
613	Verify, then report:
614	```bash
615	cd ~/DEV  # Windows: ~/Desktop/DEV
616	for r in <repos>; do printf "%-30s %s | %s\n" "$r" "$(git -C $r status -sb | head -1)" "$(git -C $r log -1 --format='%h %s' | cut -c1-60)"; done
617	```
618	Every line must show `main...origin/main` (or `master`) with no ahead/behind, and a
619	dated commit subject.
620	
621	## Step 6 — Close
622	
623	Append one line to `runs.md` (date, mode, item count, bucket counts, decided count, the
624	hidden reasons in 5 words each). Report: what was decided, where each lives, anything
625	the subagent did beyond scope, and what is left for Eric (actions only he can take).
626	
627	## Gotchas
628	
629	- Edit may be blocked in shared checkouts during background jobs; the recording
630	  subagent can fall back to a small Python string-replace that keeps line endings.
631	- Tier B `MEMORY.md` runs near its cap. Replacing a line is cheaper than adding one;
632	  check `wc -c` after every write.
633	- A repo named in docs may not exist (2026-10-02: `baylor-football-analytics` was never
634	  pushed). Verify with `gh repo view` before offering "fold it in".
635	- Machine-specific repos (e.g. `Website` lives only on the Mac): record in memory now
636	  and list "record in repo on the Mac" as a leftover.
