=================== status-report
---
name: status-report
description: >-
  Build the every-two-weeks Applied Performance status report for Kenny Boyd and Chris
  Ruf — paste-ready email, one-page PDF, internal record. Use when the user says
  "/status-report", "build my status report", "time for the Chris report", "biweekly
  update", "status update for Chris and Kenny", "what do I send Chris this week", or
  when a scheduled report date arrives. Do not use for a single meeting brief (use
  meeting-prep) or the end-of-day supervisor log interview (use interview-me).
---

# Status Report

Produce the recurring Applied Performance status report — an email to **Kenny Boyd and
Chris Ruf**, both addressed directly ("Kenny, Coach Ruf,"), every two weeks, ~270 words.

Governed by **KR 4.1** in `Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3). Read that KR as a
**content checklist** — shipped work, work in flight, decisions needed, anything at risk,
what's next — not as a layout. Eric's real reports run as flat prose with no section
headers. See **Voice** below; match it.

**Primary job: alignment.** Chris and Kenny finish the email knowing what moved, what
needs them, and what's at risk. **Secondary job: credit** — visible involvement across
sports beyond football and basketball. That secondary job is why the report was asked
for; do not let it slip out of the output.

**Design target: under 5 minutes of the user's time.** The machine does the recall. The
interview spends the user's attention only on what no system can know.

## Paths

Read `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` for all paths — never hardcode. Keys used
here: `vault_root`, `vault_inbox_meetings`, `vault_output_ledger`,
`vault_status_reports`, `vault_status_log`, `portfolio_json`, `okr_doc`, `okr_scoreboard`,
`okr_tracker_dir`, `utilization_brief`, `canonical_projects`, `fireflies_cli`.

Template: `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`
Output dir: `{vault_status_reports}`

> The config held Windows paths from the pre-migration machine until 2026-08-11. If any
> value starts with `C:\`, stop and fix the config first — every skill that trusts it is
> broken until you do.

## Relationship to other skills

- **`weekly-review` is not a prerequisite.** Never require it to have run. If review
  files exist in `Inbox/weekly-review/` for the period, read them as a bonus input; if
  they don't, proceed without comment. The report builds from primary sources so it
  cannot inherit another ritual's failure rate.
- **`meeting-sync`** may be invoked to freshen the meeting corpus, but a sync failure is
  **not** a hard stop here — fall back to `fireflies-pp-cli digest` live, and note in the
  internal record that the vault copy was stale.
- **`html-to-pdf`** renders the one-pager.

---

## Step 1 — Establish the period

Read the newest file in `{vault_status_reports}`. Period start = the previous report's
`period_end`; period end = today. If no prior report exists, period start = 14 days ago.

**Count sends.** KR 4.1's target is "≥3 **sent** by Aug 31," and writing a file is not
sending it. Count files in `{vault_status_reports}` with `sent: true` in frontmatter —
that is the real number. Report progress toward ≥3 in Step 8. If files exist with
`sent: false` older than a week, ask whether they actually went out; an uncounted send
is as bad for the KR as a missed one.

A missed send widens the period rather than skipping it. Never leave a gap in the
archive — the archive's continuity is what makes it usable as a time record.

**Cadence is settled: every two weeks.** Eric committed to it in writing in the first
report — "Starting these updates every two weeks." Report 1 went out **2026-08-24**, so
sends land on even fortnights from there (2026-09-07, 09-21, 10-05, …). The earlier
"twice monthly, 1st and 3rd Friday" plan was an assistant assumption and is retired.

## Step 2 — Pull (no user involvement)

### Step 2a — Preflight the meeting source

Run `{fireflies_cli} transcripts list --agent --data-source live 2>&1 | head -5` first.

**Fixed 2026-08-11** — the key is in `~/.zshrc` and the local mirror was rebuilt with
`fireflies-pp-cli sync`; as of 2026-08-13 the key is visible to the Bash tool directly.
The DB lives at `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db`, not `~/.fireflies-pp-cli/`.

If it fails again, `unable to open database file: out of memory (14)` means the mirror is
**missing, not corrupt** — run `sync` before anything else. Then:

- **Do not hard-stop.** `meeting-sync` hard-stops on auth failure; this skill must not,
  or it inherits the outage that already lapsed `weekly-review`.
- **Fall back** to reading `{vault_inbox_meetings}/*.md` filtered to the period by the
  `YYYY-MM-DD_` filename prefix. These files have **no YAML frontmatter** — parse the
  prepended header block (`## Key topics`, `## Decisions`, `## Action items`) and the
  Fireflies export sections (`## Summary`, `### Overview`, `### Action Items`).
- **Check staleness and say so.** Compare the newest meeting file's date to today. If
  the gap is >2 days, tell the user plainly in Step 8: *"Meeting data is stale through
  {DATE}; anything after that came only from the interview."* A silently incomplete
  report is worse than a flagged one — the user is about to send it to a supervisor.
- Record the degraded source in the internal record's frontmatter.

### Step 2b — Pull

Run these in parallel. Never ask the user for anything obtainable here.

1. **Meetings** — `{fireflies_cli} digest --since <N>d --processed-only --agent`
   (flags verified valid; `--since` accepts `7d`/`24h` form). Gives titles, gists,
   topics, and action items in one call. Cross-check against `{vault_inbox_meetings}`.
   On failure, use the 2a fallback.
1b. **Supervisor logs — read these before anything else.** Every file in
   `{vault_status_log}` whose `YYYY-MM-DD.md` filename falls inside the period. These are
   written nightly by `interview-me` Part 0 and they are the **highest-value source in
   this step**: they cover equipment, installs, hallway conversations, and follow-ups
   awaiting a reply — the operational two thirds that appears in no other source. Merge
   the three sections (`## Equipment & installs`, `## People & conversations`,
   `## Waiting on / risks`) across the period and union every `sports:` array for the
   coverage panel.

   Treat the wording as the user's own and preserve it. **Count the logged days** —
   `logged / days-in-period` gets reported in Step 8. A thin count is not a reason to
   pad; it is the number that tells the user the nightly ritual lapsed.

   Zero logs is normal for now and is **never** a hard stop — the ritual started
   2026-09-07 and the report predates it. Fall back to a full Step 4 interview.

2. **Commitments** — `{fireflies_cli} action-items list --from <N> --agent`
   (`--from` takes an integer number of days). Flag anything open >14 days; those are
   risk-section candidates. On failure, parse `## Action items` blocks from the vault
   meeting files instead.

   **Known broken as of 2026-09-07:** this command exits 0 and returns an array of empty
   `{}` objects — a serialization bug, not an empty result. Do not read it as "no open
   commitments." The digest in item 1 carries action items inline; use those and record
   the degraded source in the internal record.
3. **Shipped artifacts** — read `{vault_output_ledger}`, newest first, entries within
   the period. **This is the only source for the "Shipped" section.**

   Format is a markdown table, newest first, data rows starting at line 22:
   `| Shipped | Artifact | What it is | Harvest |` where *Shipped* is `YYYY-MM-DD`,
   *Artifact* is the short name, *What it is* is a dense paragraph, and *Harvest* holds
   `[[wikilinks]]` or is empty. Match rows with `^\| 2\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{2}` and filter by
   date. Compress *What it is* to one clause for the email — those paragraphs run long
   and will blow the 300-word ceiling if pasted whole.
4. **Project movement** — read `{portfolio_json}`, filter `lane == "job"`. Use `stage`,
   `next_action`, and `updates[]` for the *In Progress* section only.
5. **KR state** — read `{okr_doc}` (v3, 14 KRs). This is the **only** trustworthy KR
   source. Two others will lie to you:

   - **Never read the cadence doc's KR table** — superseded v2 set of 9.
   - **Do not trust `{okr_scoreboard}` for confidence values.** It was generated
     2026-06-12 against the retired *quarterly, 3-objective* set and scores KRs that no
     longer exist; v3's fourth objective (Leadership & Visibility) isn't in it at all.
     Its `Conf` decimals are real numbers attached to dead targets. If it still predates
     the v3 restructure (2026-07-17), tell the user it needs regenerating — `okrs.yaml`
     is the source of truth, `okr.py` regenerates `SCOREBOARD.md` and `okrs.json` — and
     report KR status from `{okr_doc}` alone in the meantime.

6. **Sport roster** — the 17-program list for the coverage panel comes from
   `{utilization_brief}` §"Recommendations by program" (15 rows; the two XC / Track &
   Field rows each bundle two programs). Never re-derive this list from memory. Note it
   is *prescriptive* — what each program could use — not a record of current activity,
   which is exactly why the coverage panel is worth publishing.
7. **Canonical spine** — read `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` for the confirmed
   active list, each project's sport and KR mapping.
8. **Optional** — `Inbox/weekly-review/*.md` within the period, if any exist.

### Hard rule: "Shipped" comes from the ledger, never from portfolio stage

`portfolio.json` marks projects `stage: shipped` that still have stakeholder sign-off
outstanding — Sport_Tech_Vetting is currently `shipped` while KR 1.2 shows Chris's
sign-off pending. Reporting that as shipped tells the user's supervisor that a thing he
never approved is done. **Only `_ledger.md` entries qualify as Shipped.** Portfolio
stage feeds *In Progress*.

## Voice — match the real thing, not the spec

**Read `{vault_status_reports}/2026-08-24-email-sent.txt` before drafting.** That is the
first report Eric actually sent. It is the reference for how he writes; this skill's
earlier draft was never sent and should not be imitated.

What his email actually does:

- **No section headers.** Flat short paragraphs, one topic each, no Shipped / In Progress
  / Decisions Needed labels. Do not impose the KR 4.1 headers on his prose — they are the
  *content checklist*, not the layout. Make sure each of the five things is covered
  somewhere; do not label them.
- **One framing line up top**, then straight into it. No preamble.
- **"We" for department work, "I" for his own actions.** He writes as the unit.
- **Concrete and operational.** Equipment, buildings, people, dates: Perch cameras at
  Fudge, FirstBeat monitors replacing Polar, survey cutoff August 28th. Names people
  freely — Linda, Noah, AJ, Javi, Micah.
- **Asks come last and land soft:** "One ask I wanted to run past you both is whether…"
  Do **not** convert these into "need Chris by Aug 31." That register is more forceful
  than he writes and it will read as someone else's words.
- **Stalled things get passed along, not escalated:** "still haven't heard back. Passing
  that along in case a nudge is warranted."
- **About 270 words. No attachment.** The memo PDF exists for when something needs to be
  handed across a table; the ordinary cycle is email only.

### The sourcing gap this exposed — important

Almost nothing in his real report appears in `portfolio.json` or `_ledger.md`: survey
response rates, camera installs at three buildings, heart-rate monitors arriving for
tennis, staff meeting cadence, a stalled email to Micah. Those sources track his
**building** work. He reports his **departmental operations**.

So the auto-pull covers maybe a third of what belongs in the report. **Weight the
interview accordingly** — ask about equipment, deliveries, installs, staffing, meetings
held, and follow-ups awaiting a reply, not just what moved in the registry. Treat a draft
built only from automated sources as roughly one-third finished.

## Step 3 — Draft before asking

Write a complete draft of all five sections from the pull. Cut to **5–6 projects with
real motion** — never a 14-line roster. Projects that didn't move go to the internal
record and, if relevant, the sport coverage panel.

Tag every Shipped and In Progress line with a sport: *(Volleyball)*, *(Football)*,
*(Soccer)*, *(Dept-wide)*, *(Cross-sport)*.

Then identify the gaps — that is what the interview is for.

## Step 4 — Interview the gaps only

Ask in **one batch**, not serially. Keep it to what the pull genuinely couldn't answer.
Lead with targeted gap questions, then the four standing ones.

**Targeted** (generated from the pull, examples):
- "Three meetings Tuesday–Thursday have no notes. Anything from them that Chris needs?"
- "Ledger shows nothing shipped this period — is that right, or did something go out
  that never got logged?"
- "Kinexon_Volleyball hasn't moved in the registry since July. Stalled, or just not
  logged?"

**Skip every standing question the supervisor logs already answered.** If
`{vault_status_log}` covered the period, questions 1–4 below are largely pre-filled —
read the merged log back to the user as a list and ask only *"anything missing?"* plus
questions 5–8. Re-asking what the user already typed at 9pm is how the nightly ritual
gets abandoned; the payoff for logging has to be a visibly shorter interview.

**Standing** (every time). The first three carry most of the report — they cover the
operational half no automated source sees:

1. **Equipment, installs, deliveries.** What arrived, what got installed where, what's
   being phased out, who's onboarding onto it. Eric's real reports lead with this
   (Perch cameras at Fudge, FirstBeat monitors replacing Polar for tennis).
2. **Meetings held and staffing.** Who he met with, what came out of it, changes to
   cadence or who attends. Names matter — Linda, Noah, AJ, Javi.
3. **Conversations no transcript caught** — hallway, text, sideline, phone. Invisible to
   every automated source, and among the highest-value things this interview captures.
4. **Anything waiting on someone else.** Unanswered emails, pending approvals, stalled
   follow-ups. These become the soft "passing that along" lines at the end.
5. **Anything about to go sideways** that Chris and Kenny should hear from him first.
   *(Push here. An always-empty risk line means it isn't being used honestly.)*
6. **Any ask** — time at a meeting, a decision, a nudge. Phrased softly, at the end.
7. **Ideas generated** — worth parking, pitching, or building?
8. **What's next** for the coming two weeks.

Also ask, if the pull shows thin coverage: *"Any sport you touched this period that
isn't showing up in my sources?"* Non-revenue involvement is the whole point and it is
the most likely thing to be undercounted.

## Step 5 — Assemble and check

Fill the template at `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`.

Run every check before showing the user anything:

- [ ] **Email body is under 300 words.** Count it. State the count. Over the ceiling,
      cut — do not negotiate with yourself.
- [ ] **Every Shipped line traces to a `_ledger.md` entry.** No exceptions.
- [ ] **No endorsement claimed that doesn't exist.** If sign-off is pending, "our
      standard intake process," never "the approved process."
- [ ] **Every Shipped and In Progress line carries a sport tag.**
- [ ] **Every Decisions Needed item names a person and a date.** No owner or no date
      means it isn't a decision request — rewrite or cut it.
- [ ] **Jargon table enforced.** No CMJ, ACWR, asymmetry index, unexplained B.A.I.R.
- [ ] **Department names.** Athletic Performance (not strength and conditioning / S&C),
      Athletic Medicine (not sports medicine), Applied Performance (not sport science).
- [ ] **Never "one unified dashboard."** The line is "standardized underneath, bespoke
      on top."
- [ ] **Research presented as research** — no readiness or deployment claims.
- [ ] **Risks section is non-empty** unless the user explicitly confirmed there's
      nothing. Ask once more before letting it go empty.
- [ ] **Repeat check:** any Decisions Needed item carried over from the previous report
      gets flagged to the user — two unanswered asks means the email has failed at it
      and it needs raising in person.
- [ ] **Email and PDF agree.** The two are filled separately, so verify it: every
      Shipped, In Progress, Decisions Needed, and Risks item in the email appears in the
      PDF. The PDF may carry *more* detail — it must never carry different facts, a
      different sport tag, or a different date. Sending a supervisor two versions of the
      same report is the failure this check exists to prevent.
- [ ] **Sport coverage panel is not padded.** Untouched sports stay marked untouched. A
      thin panel is real information; a padded one destroys the evidentiary value of
      every honest panel before and after it.

**Loop until clean.** Any failed box: fix the draft, then run the whole list again from
the top — a cut for word count can drop a sport tag or the only risk line. Show the user
the draft only after one full pass with every box ticked.

## Step 6 — Emit

Produce three things:

1. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-status.md`** — the internal record, full Layer 3
   structure from the template: email as sent, meetings held, conversations, ideas, full
   roster, KR ledger, and the "Not for the report" candid section.
2. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.pdf`** — render
   `assets/one-pager.html` with the period's content. One page, always.

   **It is a printed memorandum, not a dashboard.** Single column, one serif family,
   letterspaced small-cap section heads, one green hairline. Never reintroduce status
   dots, badge or pill rows, bolded stat lines, progress bars, or a two-column grid —
   that vocabulary is what made the first version read as generated.

   **Measure before shipping**, don't eyeball it. Budget is **950px of content at 666px
   width**:

   ```bash
   python3 -c "s=open('<file>.html').read(); open('/tmp/probe.html','w').write(
     s.replace('</body>','<script>window.addEventListener(\"load\",()=>{document.title=
     \"H:\"+Math.round(document.body.getBoundingClientRect().height)})</script></body>'))"
   "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless --disable-gpu \
     --virtual-time-budget=3000 --window-size=666,1200 --dump-dom file:///tmp/probe.html \
     | grep -o '<title>H:[0-9]*'
   ```

   Then render: `--headless --disable-gpu --no-pdf-header-footer --print-to-pdf=<out>`.
   Over 950px, **cut prose** — never drop below 9.6pt. This gets printed and read by
   people who will not squint for you.
3. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-email.txt`** — the email body as **plain text**,
   the file the user actually touches each cycle. Strip all markdown: no `**bold**`, no
   `-` bullets rendered as syntax. Use `•` or plain indentation, and spell section
   headers in caps (`SHIPPED`, `IN PROGRESS`). Outlook's compose window pastes markdown
   asterisks literally, and a supervisor email full of `**` reads as carelessness.
   Select-all-copy from this file should produce something sendable with zero cleanup.
4. **Also print the email text in the response** so the user can read it without opening
   a file — but the `.txt` is the artifact of record for sending.

### Do not send

The connected Gmail account is the user's **personal** address
(`eric.rash11@gmail.com`), not Baylor. Do not create Gmail drafts — they would land in
the wrong mailbox. The user sends from Outlook on the work account.

Never send a report to a supervisor without the user reading it first, under any
circumstance.

## Step 7 — Log

- Append shipped artifacts to `{vault_output_ledger}` if the interview surfaced any that
  weren't logged.
- Update `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` with confirmed status, sport, and KR
  mapping — this keeps the canonical spine current as a byproduct rather than a chore.
- Add an `updates[]` entry to `{portfolio_json}` for each project reported as moved, via
  the `project` skill, so the registry stops being empty.
- Set `sent: false` in the internal record. The user flips it after sending.

## Step 8 — Report to the user

State: word count, report number, next send date, which sports appeared, anything the
checks flagged, and where the three files landed.

Also state **`N of D` days logged** in `{vault_status_log}` for the period. Say it
plainly and without nagging — the number is the nudge. When the count is low, say what it
cost: *"6 of 14 days logged, so the interview had to cover the other 8 from memory."*

**Propose a rule when one was missing.** If this run hit a problem no Step 5 box covers —
caught by you, or by Eric editing the draft before sending — end with one proposed new
checklist line and the reason. Add it to Step 5 only on Eric's yes; the next report is
then checked against it.

---

## Failure modes to design against

**Padding.** A thin period is a legitimate output. "Nothing shipped this period" is an
honest line that protects the word "shipped" everywhere else. Inflating a quiet period
is the fastest way to make the report worthless — and to make the time documentation
inadmissible when it matters.

**Roster creep.** The email is not a project list. 14 status lines reads as 14 things
half-done. Five moving projects reads as focus.

**The credit goal quietly disappearing.** The report exists so non-football,
non-basketball involvement becomes visible. If a period's coverage panel is thin, that
is real information and it should be shown, not hidden — a padded panel destroys the
evidentiary value of every honest one.

**Depending on another ritual.** `weekly-review` lapsed for seven weeks earlier this
year. This report must never require it.
=================== capture-insight
---
name: capture-insight
description: >-
  Capture a story, win, or lesson the user just shared as a permanent atomic note in the
  SecondBrain vault. Use when the user tells a story or lesson and says "capture this",
  "save this win/lesson", "that's worth a note", or "/capture-insight". Do not use for
  end-of-day structured capture (use interview-me), whole-project distillation (use
  harvest), or plain facts (use memory-write).
---

# Capture Insight

Write one atomic permanent note in `vault_notes` from the selected platform config from something the user just shared. Capturing is the point — write it, then confirm.

**Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` (`vault_notes`) — load it if unsure; if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins.

## Format

Follow the vault's atomic-note format (see any existing `Notes/*.md`):

- Frontmatter: `type: permanent, created, source, domain, tags, status: seed`
- Kebab-case filename
- A `# Title` that states the insight **as a claim**
- A blockquote distillation, then a short body
- Wikilink related existing notes

## Rules

- One note per distinct insight; bias toward fewer, sharper notes.
- Confirm with the file path and the claim it captures.
- If what was shared is a plain fact or preference rather than an insight, route to memory-write instead.
=================== harvest
---
name: harvest
description: >-
  Distill a finished project into evergreen Knowledge/ articles in the SecondBrain vault
  and log the shipped artifact in the output ledger. Use when the user says "/harvest
  <project>", "harvest this project", "distill what we learned from X", declares a
  project finished/shipped/done, or when a session ends with a clearly shipped
  deliverable worth recording. Do not use for a single story or lesson (use
  capture-insight) or for the end-of-session sign-off (use closeout).
argument-hint: "[project]"
---

# Harvest

Turn a **finished** project into (1) an entry in the shipped-work ledger and
(2) zero or more evergreen lesson articles in `Knowledge/`.

**Vault:** `vault_root` in the selected platform config (conventions: vault `CLAUDE.md`)
**Ledger:** `output/_ledger.md`
**Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` — load it if unsure; if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins.

Core rule: lesson articles are written ONLY from shipped work. If the project
hasn't shipped, stop — offer to note it in `Projects/` instead.

## Process

### 1. Confirm the ship

Establish: what shipped, when, and the evidence (deliverable handed off, talk
given, pipeline live, commit/PR, decision locked). If Eric declared it shipped,
that's sufficient — record his framing. If ambiguous ("mostly done"), ask one
question; a harvest of unfinished work poisons the ledger.

### 2. Gather the project's story

Pull from whichever exist, cheapest first:

- The project folder (DEV repo, vault `Projects/` folder) — plans, READMEs, retro notes
- `memsearch search "<project> lessons decisions" --top-k 5` — session history
- The current conversation, if the project just finished here

You're looking for: what was tried and abandoned, what surprised, what the
final approach was and *why*, what broke and how it was diagnosed.

### 3. Append the ledger entry (always)

Add a row to `output/_ledger.md`, newest first:
`| YYYY-MM-DD | artifact | one-line description | [[harvest-article-slug]] or empty |`

This step always happens. Steps 4–5 only happen if lessons clear the bar.

### 4. Distill lessons (0–3 articles, only when earned)

The bar: **a lesson qualifies only if it would change how a future, unrelated
project is done.** "We built X with Y" is ledger material, not a lesson.
"Schedulers fail silently unless the task itself writes a heartbeat" is a lesson.
Zero qualifying lessons is a legitimate outcome — say so and stop after the ledger.

Each article: one idea, kebab-case filename, into `Knowledge/` (subfolder by
kind if one fits, e.g. `Knowledge/frameworks/`):

```markdown
---
type: harvest
created: YYYY-MM-DD
source: <project name + repo/folder path>
shipped: YYYY-MM-DD
domain: [one, two]
tags: [three, four]
status: evergreen
---

# <The lesson as a claim, not a topic>

> **Harvested from:** <project> (shipped <date>)
> **In one sentence:** <the lesson>

<3–10 sentences: the context that produced it, why the obvious approach
failed or the chosen one worked, and where else this applies. Write it so
it makes sense to someone who never saw the project.>
```

### 5. Cross-link

- Wikilink first mentions of concepts/people/projects that have existing notes
  (scan filenames across `Notes/`, `Knowledge/`, `Projects/`).
- Add a `## Related` section (2–5 genuinely related links).
- Backfill the ledger row's harvest column with `[[article-slug]]`.

### 6. Close out

- If the project has a vault `Projects/` file, mark its status shipped/harvested.
- Commit the vault changes (ledger + articles) with message `harvest: <project>`.
- Report in one short paragraph: ledger entry, articles written (or "no lessons
  cleared the bar"), links added.

## Rules

- **Never overwrite** an existing note; slug collision → `-2` or ask to merge.
- Never harvest unfinished work. Never write a lesson article outside a harvest
  (that's the vault's harvest rule, see vault `CLAUDE.md`).
- Lessons are what was *learned*; the ledger records what was *done*. Don't mix.
- Prefer 1 sharp article over 3 mushy ones. Zero is fine.

# Ingest Resource

Turn any incoming resource into a well-placed, summarized, cross-linked vault note.

**Vault:** `vault_root` in the selected platform config
**Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` — load it if unsure; if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins.

## Process

### 1. Acquire the content

| Input | How to get content |
|-------|-------------------|
| Article URL | WebFetch first; if empty/JS-shell, use web-scraping skill's `firecrawl_scrape.py -o tmp.md` |
| YouTube link | WebFetch the page for title/channel/description; ask user to paste transcript if the content itself is needed |
| PDF | Read tool (use `pages` for long PDFs) |
| Pasted transcript / note | Already in hand |
| Local file path | Read it |

### 2. Route it

Decide by **shelf life**, not topic:

- **`Knowledge/`** — stable reference that will still be true in a year: frameworks, mental models, voice/style guides, people profiles, processes, how-tos. Subfolder by kind: `Knowledge/frameworks/`, `Knowledge/people/`, `Knowledge/processes/`, `Knowledge/voice/` (add others as needed).
- **`Projects/`** — fuel for active work: video research, newsletter material, launch assets, anything tied to a current effort. If it belongs to an existing project file/folder (`Project_*.md`, `Graphify/`, etc.), place it alongside; otherwise drop it in `Projects/` root with a clear name.

Create any folder that doesn't exist yet (`New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force`). If routing is genuinely ambiguous, ask one question; otherwise decide and say why.

### 3. Write the note

Filename: kebab-case slug of the title (vault convention). Format:

```markdown
---
type: resource
created: YYYY-MM-DD
source: <URL, "PDF: filename", or "conversation">
domain: [one, two]
tags: [three, four]
status: ingested
---

# Title

> **Summary**
> **Source:** <link or origin> · **Date:** <published or ingested date>
> **Key people:** [[Person One]], Person Two
> **Key concepts:** concept one, concept two, concept three
>
> 2–4 sentence digest of what this is and why it was kept.

<full content or distilled body>
```

### 4. Cross-link

- List existing note names: filenames (sans `.md`) across `Notes/`, `Knowledge/`, `Projects/`.
- In the new note's body, wikilink the **first mention** of any concept/person/project that matches an existing note: `[[adoption-is-the-bottleneck]]` or `[[Project_AI-Integration|AI Integration]]`.
- Link related-but-not-mentioned notes in a `## Related` section at the bottom (2–5 links max, only genuinely related).
- A `[[wikilink]]` to a note that doesn't exist yet is fine for key people/concepts worth a future note — use sparingly.

### 5. Confirm

Report: file path, route chosen (and why), links added. One short paragraph.

## Rules

- **Never overwrite** an existing note — if the slug collides, append `-2` or merge after asking.
- Long sources (>2,000 words): keep the full text in the body but make the summary block self-sufficient.
- Don't route to `Notes/` — that folder is for synthesized permanent notes (interview-me's territory), not raw resources.
- Don't route to `Inbox/` — ingestion IS the processing step; the note lands in its final home.

## Verification Gate

After writing the note:

1. Read it back and verify the destination path, route, frontmatter, summary block, full-source body, and related-links section are present as applicable.
2. Compare the summary with the source. Require all named people, numbers, dates, quotations, and conclusions to preserve the source's meaning and attribution.
3. Confirm the new note did not overwrite an unrelated file and that the final slug is unique.
4. Check each wikilink target. Existing-note links must resolve; intentional future-note links must be labeled as such in the verification result.

Report `PASS` only when the written note matches the source and all filesystem checks succeed. Report `FAIL` for missing source content, altered claims, an overwrite, or a broken link presented as existing. Report `DEGRADED` when the source could not be fully accessed and identify what was summarized from partial evidence.

# Ingest Book

Turn a book into atomized, citable entries under the library subtree, grouped by domain and book, ready for the `advisor` skill.

**Library root:** `vault_library` in the selected platform config
**Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` (`vault_library`, `vault_root`) — load it if unsure; if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins.
**Extractors:** `~/.claude/skills/ingest-book/lib/extract_epub.py`, `extract_pdf.py`
Run extractors inside the context-mode sandbox (`ctx_execute`, language python) so raw book text never enters the conversation — only the atomized entries you write do.

## Model split (cost vs quality)

This skill mixes three kinds of work with very different model needs:
- **Extraction & structure mapping** (probe, chapter map, text cleanup) — deterministic
  Python in the sandbox. **Zero model tokens; model choice irrelevant.**
- **Orchestration** (searches, `_book.md` updates, dedup checks) — mechanical.
  **Haiku-tier is fine.**
- **Atomization** (Phase 2/3: distilling prose into accurate entries with correct
  mechanism-vs-claim, honest confidence, and a real "when NOT to apply") — this is where
  the advisor's entire value is created. **Run on Sonnet or stronger. Do NOT use Haiku
  for atomization** — a weak distillation becomes a permanent low-quality entry, and the
  generated output is only ~3K tokens/chapter, so quality-per-token matters far more than
  price-per-token. Cost levers that DON'T hurt quality: atomize only chapters you'll
  consult, and checkpoint + `/clear` between chapter batches (see Rules) so context
  doesn't compound across the book.

## Schema for every entry note

Filename: `<kind>--<kebab-slug>.md`, `kind ∈ {principle, framework, case-study, heuristic, claim}`.

```yaml
---
type: library-entry
kind: principle
domain: <domain-slug>
book: <book-slug>
chapter: "N"            # or section label; "" if highlights with no location
topic: <2-5 word topic>
category: [tag, tag]
confidence: proven      # proven | supported | untested | contested
ingest-tier: full-text  # full-text | highlights | framework-only
created: <YYYY-MM-DD>
---

# <Human title of the idea>

**What it is** — one tight paragraph.
**Why it works** — mechanism, not restatement.
**When to apply** — concrete triggers.
**When NOT to apply** — scope limits. (MANDATORY — never omit.)
**Example** — one concrete instance.
```

**Confidence is bounded by tier:** full-text ≤ proven; highlights ≤ supported;
framework-only ≤ untested. Set `contested` by hand when sources conflict.

## Phase 1 — Intake

1. Identify: book title, author, source type (PDF/EPUB | Kindle highlights | physical), target domain.
2. Compute `<book-slug>` = `kebab(title)--kebab(lastname)` (e.g. `supertraining--verkhoshansky`).
3. If the domain folder/`_domain.md` doesn't exist, create them (mirror the S&C `_domain.md` format).
4. Build `_book.md` chapter map:
   - EPUB/PDF: run the extractor with `--list` / `--probe` to get the chapter or page structure.
   - Physical: ask the user for the chapter list, or assemble from a verified public listing.
   Write `_book.md` (template below) with every chapter `status: pending`.

`_book.md` template:
```markdown
---
type: book-index
book: <book-slug>
title: <full title>
author: <author>
domain: <domain-slug>
ingest-tier: full-text | highlights | framework-only
source: "<file path or 'physical' or 'kindle-highlights'>"
created: <YYYY-MM-DD>
---

# <title> — ingest map

| # | Chapter | Status | Entries |
|---|---------|--------|---------|
| 0 | <title> | pending | 0 |
```

## Phase 2 — Extract (by tier)

**Full-text (PDF/EPUB):**
- First run `extract_pdf.py --probe`. If `scanned: true`, STOP the full-text path:
  tell the user the PDF is image-only, and fall back to framework-only tier (set
  `ingest-tier: framework-only`, cap confidence at untested). Never emit full-text-
  confidence entries from a scanned file.
- Work **one chapter at a time** (EPUB `--chapter N`; PDF `--pages A-B`, where A and B are
  0-based PDF indexes and the range is inclusive: `--pages 12-20` returns 9 pages). Each page
  comes back with `page` (0-based index) and `viewer_page` (what a PDF viewer shows, index + 1).
  Cite pages one way throughout a book and state the convention in `_book.md`. For each:
  extract candidate ideas → atomize per the schema → write entry notes.
- **After each chapter**, update that row in `_book.md` to `status: done` with the
  entry count. This is the resume checkpoint — never batch this update.

**Kindle highlights:**
- Parse `My Clippings.txt` or the highlights export in the sandbox. Cluster highlights
  by theme; write one entry per theme. `ingest-tier: highlights`, confidence ≤ supported.
- Attribute `chapter` from the highlight's location metadata when present, else "".

**Framework-only (physical / scanned):**
- Briefly interview the user for their takeaways. Supplement with *verified* public
  chapter summaries. Write 5–15 framework-level entries. `ingest-tier: framework-only`,
  confidence ≤ untested.

## Phase 3 — Quality gate (run before writing each batch)

- One idea per note. If an extracted point is compound, split it.
- "When NOT to apply" present and non-trivial.
- **Dedup + converge:** before writing, `memsearch search` the library for the same
  concept. If an existing entry (any book) covers it, DON'T duplicate — instead add a
  `[[wikilink]]` + one line to both notes recording the agreement, and only add a new
  note if it contributes a genuinely new angle.
- Never overwrite an existing file; on slug collision append `-2`.

## Phase 4 — Close-out

1. Set all done rows in `_book.md`; if partial, leave pending rows for next session.
2. Add the book to `_domain.md`'s `books:` list and the "Books in this domain" section.
3. Add the book-slug to the advisor persona's `books:` list (`advisors/<domain>.md`)
   if an advisor exists.
4. Run `memsearch index "<vault_library>"` using the selected platform config
   so entries are searchable immediately (don't wait for the SessionEnd hook).
5. Commit the vault using `vault_root` from the selected platform config: `git -C "<vault_root>" add Knowledge/library && git commit -m "ingest(<book-slug>): <N> entries, ch X-Y"`.
6. Report: entries by kind and confidence, links created, chapters remaining.

## Rules
- Raw book text stays in the sandbox; only atomized entries enter context/the vault.
- Resumable by design: `_book.md` is the source of truth for "where am I".
- A 300-page book is a multi-session job — stop at a chapter boundary, never mid-chapter.

name: research-in-5
description: "Build a \"Research in 5\" weekly paper review for Baylor Athletics staff: a 5-slide deck (dark and light), a Teams post, and a staff email from one paper. Use when the user says \"/research-in-5\", \"research in 5 on this paper\", \"weekly research review\", \"review this paper for the staff\", \"make the slides for this paper\", hands over a paper (PDF, DOI, URL, Zotero item), or wants a review rebuilt or versioned (#001, v2). Do not use for a sport-science question (use sports-science-research-grounding), a deck with no single paper (use five-slides-generator), or a plain Zotero search."

# Research in 5

The procedure, content rules, and build tooling live in the project repo, not here.
This skill gets you into the repo and carries the lessons that are easy to relearn
the hard way.

## Start

1. Project root: `~/Desktop/DEV/Weekly_Research_Review` (Windows) or
   `~/DEV/Weekly_Research_Review` (Mac). Missing on this machine:
   `gh repo clone erash11/Weekly_Research_Review` into DEV.
2. `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, and
   `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`. Follow WORKFLOW.md step by step; it owns the process.
3. Background session: work in a worktree of that repo, open a PR, merge only when
   Eric says so.

Build and QA: `pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug -NoDrive`, read every
`dark-slideN.png` and `light-slideN.png`, then publish without `-NoDrive`.
Deliverables land in `07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5/NNN_slug/` on the Google Drive
primary storage drive.

## Gotchas

- **Check Zotero for the full text before settling for an abstract.** A new item's PDF may not be indexed yet: run `sync_zotero_library` with `include_fulltext: true`, then `get_paper` and look at `attachments`. #001 was first built from the abstract while the PDF sat in Zotero.
- **Article-in-press papers often have no public PDF.** Springer's PDF URL 404s even in Chrome. Ask Eric for the PDF or check Zotero; set `paper.full_text: false` only as a last resort and say so in the post.
- **Every number comes from the paper's tables, with a page, as reported.** Write `notes.md` first. Plot and tabulate exact values; never display a computed difference. Flag contradictions inside the paper (a conclusion stronger than its own limitations, a mislabeled table) in notes.md.
- **Slides carry one idea each; detail goes to the post.** Slide-facing fields have tight limits that build.js enforces (question 90, fact 26, summary 110, role line 70, takeaway 60, bottom line 55). Write those short first. `did.bullets`, `results.bullets`, extra limitations, and the discussion question are post-only.
- **Department names:** Athletic Performance (not strength and conditioning), Athletic Medicine (not sports medicine), Applied Performance (not sport science). build.js rejects others.
- **Baylor Bears Font has only A to Z, 0 to 9, space and `. : ! - #`.** It sets display text only; `headline` must fit that set. Section titles are caps statements because there is no `?`. Agency FB sets everything people read and has no `→`.
- **"Calibri" in the PDF font list is expected.** PowerPoint cannot embed Bears (OpenType-CFF) and draws it as outlines with a Calibri-tagged text layer. Only `Agency FB embedded: False` is a real failure. Both fonts must be installed before building on a new machine (`DEV/Baylor_Fonts`).
- **Run the humanizer skill on the audience copy before the final build.** Keep facts, pages, and limits; cut rule-of-three lists, "not X, but Y" lines, and stacked rhetorical questions.
- **Revisions get a new `version`** (outputs `_vN`) so the files Eric may already have shared stay on Drive. Only overwrite in place for a same-day correction, and say so.
- **The deck is checked against the paper before it can publish.** Step 5 runs `pwsh tools/verify.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug`; `publish.ps1` runs it again and refuses to copy anything to Drive on a real finding. Three outcomes: **VERIFY FAIL** means a claim is fabricated, contradicted, unsupported, or on the wrong page, so fix review.json and rebuild. **VERIFY PASS** may still name claims needing a human read - those are the `[REVIEW]` lines, where the model was not confident enough to decide, and you read them against notes.md. **VERIFY DEGRADED** means the check could not run at all (it needs the `TypeSafe_Sandbox` clone, its venv, and `~/.claude/typesafe.env`); it does not block, but report it like a DEGRADED image QA - the deck went out unchecked. `-SkipVerify` bypasses the gate; only use it after checking by hand, and say so.
- **publish.ps1 needs Windows PowerShell COM (installed PowerPoint) for the PDF export.** On the Mac, `node tools/build.js` still builds the pptx files and posts; export and publish from the Windows laptop.
- **Eric prefers the dark deck.** Both themes build every run; send the dark PDF first.
- **Loop until verify passes.** VERIFY FAIL or a bad PNG: fix review.json, rebuild, and run `verify.ps1` and the image read again — never publish on a fix that hasn't been re-checked.
- **Propose a rule when one was missing.** If a problem got past build.js and verify.ps1 (caught in the PNG read, the humanizer pass, or by Eric), end the run by proposing one new gotcha line here or one new check in `CONTENT_SPEC.md`, with the reason. Add it only on Eric's yes.

## Examples

```
User: "Research in 5 on this one: Saraee 2026, J Orthop Surg Res, alignment and jumper's knee"
→ cd into the repo, pull, read STATUS
→ Zotero: search, sync with full text, read every page; write notes.md
→ review.json (next number), humanizer pass, publish.ps1 -NoDrive, verify.ps1, read all PNGs
→ publish, commit on a branch, PR; send the dark PDF, teams.md, email.txt
```

```
User: "Make #001 less busy" / "use our department names" / "make a v2"
→ edit review.json or tools/build.js, bump version, rebuild both themes, QA, PR
```

---
name: memory-write
description: >-
  Writes, updates, removes, and recalls facts in the two-tier memory system
  (~/.claude/global-memory/ and ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/). Use for write
  requests such as "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", and
  "forget about", and for recall requests such as "did we already…?", "what did we
  decide about X?", and "do you remember…?". Picks the tier, dedups, and enforces caps;
  recall checks the injected snapshot, then memsearch. Do not use for a story or lesson
  worth a vault note (use capture-insight) or an article to keep (use ingest-resource).
---

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.
=================== claude-stack-doctor
---
name: claude-stack-doctor
description: >-
  Health-check Eric's automation/memory stack in one pass and verify the Mac-to-Windows
  handoff works: launchd agents / Windows scheduled tasks, Python venvs, memsearch, the memory-compiler flush
  pipeline, backup freshness, and context budget. Use when the user says
  "/claude-stack-doctor", "stack doctor", "is my stack healthy", "did my scheduled jobs
  run", "check the memory pipeline", "why didn't the backup run", or when
  closeout/morning sessions should verify automation health. Do not use to run the
  backup itself (use backup) or to audit context-engineering practice (use doctor-plus).
---

# Claude Stack Doctor

One command surfaces every known silent-failure class in the automation/memory stack. Run it before debugging anything by hand.

## Quick start

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor/scripts/stack-check.ps1   # Mac
pwsh -NoProfile -File $HOME\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\stack-check.ps1                 # Windows
```

The same script runs on both machines and picks its checks by OS (see **Two machines** below). On Windows use `pwsh` 7, not `powershell` 5.1, which reports false `memsearch-run` / `backup-cloud-check` failures.

Exit 0 = all clear. Exit 1 = the VERDICT line lists issue codes. Report the findings to the user, then apply the matching fix below.

## Cross-machine handoff (runs on BOTH machines)

`scripts/handoff-check.ps1` is called at the end of `stack-check.ps1`, and it can also be run on its own:

```
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\handoff-check.ps1
```

It answers a question nothing else here asked: did state actually make the trip between the two machines? Every other check verifies a component. This verifies the path.

The failure it exists to catch: `daily-backup` pushes `global-memory` nightly and, until 2026-09-12, nothing on the receiving machine ever pulled it. The Windows laptop was found 4 commits behind with every other signal reading healthy, because the backup section measures `ahead` only — which catches a broken push and is blind to a missing pull.

Issue codes:

- `handoff-memory-stale` — `global-memory` is behind origin. This is the serious one: memory written on the other machine is on GitHub and not here, so this session is running on stale context. Fix with `/startup`, or `git -C ~/.claude/global-memory pull --no-rebase`.
- `handoff-behind:<repo>` — config, skills or notes behind origin. Same fix, lower stakes.
- `handoff-unpushed:<repo>` — this machine is more than 3 commits ahead. The other machine cannot see this work; run `/closeout`.
- `handoff-fetch:<repo>` — offline, or GitHub auth has rotted.
- `handoff-repo-gone:<repo>` — the folder is present but is not a git repo. Something replaced a synced repo with a plain folder and its contents are going nowhere.
- A repo absent from the machine entirely is skipped, not failed. `SecondBrain` is Mac-only and its absence on Windows is correct.

The "memory flow" line reports how long since `origin/main` on `global-memory` last advanced. Over 14 days it says so without failing: it cannot distinguish "quiet fortnight" from "the other machine's backup stopped pushing", and a check that cries wolf during the first gets ignored during the second.

## Two machines

`stack-check.ps1` tests `$env:OS -eq 'Windows_NT'` and swaps the machine-specific sections. Everything else (memsearch, flush pipeline, memory repos, cloud receipt, context budget, handoff) is shared.

| Section | Mac | Windows laptop |
|---|---|---|
| Jobs | launchd `com.keystone.*` agents | Task Scheduler: `Backup AI Sessions to Drive`, `DailyGmailDigest`, `CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder` (disabled tasks are skipped) |
| venv | `.venv/bin/python` | `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` |
| memsearch backend | — | Docker Desktop `milvus-standalone` must be `(healthy)` |
| Backup state | `backup-state.json` (daily-backup) | `backup-ai-sessions-state.json` (daily). `Desktop\DEV` itself is a Drive for Desktop synced root; its weekly robocopy task was retired 2026-09-22 (XML in `~/.claude/scripts/retired/`) |
| SecondBrain | checked | skipped, it is Mac-only |

Windows issue codes:
- `task:<name>`: the last run exited non-zero. `3221225786` (0xC000013A, sleep/shutdown kill) only warns; the age check decides whether the job is really behind.
- `task-stale:<name>`, `task-never-run:<name>`, `task-missing:<name>`: the job is behind, has never run, or was deleted. Tasks live under `\Eric\`. Re-run with `Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName '<name>' | Start-ScheduledTask`; a bare `Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName` fails with "cannot find the file specified".
- `task-dual-run:<name>`: a `KeystoneOS-*` task is enabled on Windows. The Mac owns those jobs and the data pulls; disable the Windows copy.
- `milvus-docker` / `milvus-down`: start Docker Desktop; memsearch hooks time out without it.
- `backup-missing:<tag>`, `backup-stale:<tag>`, `backup-error:<tag>`: read `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\05_SYSTEMS\AI_Sessions_Backup\<COMPUTERNAME>\_backup_log.txt`. The script silences robocopy, so re-run the robocopy line in the foreground to see which files failed (codes below 8 are success).

On the Windows laptop the weekly run is Task Scheduler task `\Eric\KeystoneOS-StackDoctor` (Mondays 10:30, pwsh 7). It is the one `KeystoneOS-*` task that stays enabled on Windows.

**Mac notes.** Jobs are **launchd user agents** in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`. The script is PowerShell because `pwsh` runs it natively on both machines. PowerShell on macOS normalises `\` inside a path string to `/`, so the script's mixed separators resolve correctly — verified 2026-08-29. Do not "fix" them.

Useful launchd commands:
```bash
launchctl list | grep keystone                                    # loaded jobs + last exit code
launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.<name>                  # live schedule and state
launchctl bootout  gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.<name>               # unload
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.<name>.plist   # reload
```
Edit a schedule with `/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :StartCalendarInterval:Hour <n>" <plist>`, then bootout + bootstrap. **A plist edit alone does nothing until it is reloaded.**

## Weekly scheduled run

launchd agent `com.keystone.stackdoctor` (Mondays 10:30) runs `scripts/weekly-check.ps1`: the same read-only check, unattended. On failure it appends a one-line summary to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` (surfaced at every session start per CLAUDE.md) and the full output is always in `scripts/last-weekly-run.log`. When a session surfaces such an entry, run this skill interactively to diagnose and fix, then clear the entry from `.errors.log`.

**Clearing `.errors.log`:** shell truncation (`: > file`) anywhere under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`. Use `cp /dev/null <file>`. There is no `truncate` binary on this machine. Archive first — the lines are often live issues, not stale history:
```bash
cp ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log.archived-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
```

## Known failure classes and fixes

These four classes have each bitten more than once (evidence: daily logs 2026-04 → 2026-07). Match the issue code to its fix:

### `task:*` / `task-stale:*` — launchd agent failed or didn't run
1. Read the `action:` line the script printed and run that exact command **manually in a foreground terminal** — launchd discards stdout unless the plist sets `StandardOutPath`; foreground shows the real error.
2. Known root causes: executable referenced without a full path (launchd agents get a minimal PATH — always use full paths like `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh`, and set `EnvironmentVariables:PATH` in the plist); a plist edited but never `bootout`+`bootstrap`ed, so the old schedule is still live; the job firing at an hour the required volume is unmounted (see `backup-*`).
3. `launchctl list | grep keystone` shows each job's **last exit code** in column 2. A non-zero there with no output means the script's own log is the only evidence — check `~/.claude/scripts/logs/` and for a `*.log` beside the script.

### `venv-missing` / `venv-broken` — Python venv rot
The script checks `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/.venv/bin/python`.
macOS root causes: a Homebrew `python3` major-version bump orphans venvs built against the old interpreter; a `uv` reinstall or relocation breaks tools that hardcode `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv` (CLAUDE.md forbids relocating it for this reason).
Fix: recreate the venv (`uv sync` in the project, or `python3 -m venv .venv` + reinstall from its pyproject), then run the dependent agent once by hand to confirm.
*History (Windows box, retired 2026-08-14): Python Install Manager migrations deleted `C:\Python31x` twice, silently killing morning-briefing for 6 days. The lesson transfers — an interpreter move breaks every venv built on it — the paths do not.*

### `memsearch-path` / `memsearch-run` — memsearch CLI broken
memsearch is a **uv tool** on this machine: binary at `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/memsearch`, environment at `/Users/kristinarash/.local/share/uv/tools/memsearch/`.
- Not on PATH or the binary errors → reinstall with `uv tool install --force memsearch`, not pip.
- Import failures inside the tool env (e.g. `onnxruntime`) are testable directly:
  `/Users/kristinarash/

1	=================== ingest-book
2	---
3	name: ingest-book
4	description: >-
5	  Ingest a book (PDF/EPUB full-text, Kindle highlights, or framework-only from a
6	  physical book) into the SecondBrain library as atomized, citable advisor entries. Use
7	  when the user wants to "ingest a book", "add a book to my library/advisors",
8	  "/ingest-book", or points at a book file for the advisor system. Do not use for
9	  articles, transcripts, or general resources (use ingest-resource).
10	argument-hint: "[book file or title] [domain]"
11	---
12	
13	# Ingest Book
14	
15	Turn a book into atomized, citable entries under the library subtree, grouped by domain and book, ready for the `advisor` skill.
16	
17	**Library root:** `vault_library` in the selected platform config
18	**Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` (`vault_library`, `vault_root`) — load it if unsure; if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins.
19	**Extractors:** `~/.claude/skills/ingest-book/lib/extract_epub.py`, `extract_pdf.py`
20	Run extractors inside the context-mode sandbox (`ctx_execute`, language python) so raw book text never enters the conversation — only the atomized entries you write do.
21	
22	## Model split (cost vs quality)
23	
24	This skill mixes three kinds of work with very different model needs:
25	- **Extraction & structure mapping** (probe, chapter map, text cleanup) — deterministic
26	  Python in the sandbox. **Zero model tokens; model choice irrelevant.**
27	- **Orchestration** (searches, `_book.md` updates, dedup checks) — mechanical.
28	  **Haiku-tier is fine.**
29	- **Atomization** (Phase 2/3: distilling prose into accurate entries with correct
30	  mechanism-vs-claim, honest confidence, and a real "when NOT to apply") — this is where
31	  the advisor's entire value is created. **Run on Sonnet or stronger. Do NOT use Haiku
32	  for atomization** — a weak distillation becomes a permanent low-quality entry, and the
33	  generated output is only ~3K tokens/chapter, so quality-per-token matters far more than
34	  price-per-token. Cost levers that DON'T hurt quality: atomize only chapters you'll
35	  consult, and checkpoint + `/clear` between chapter batches (see Rules) so context
36	  doesn't compound across the book.
37	
38	## Schema for every entry note
39	
40	Filename: `<kind>--<kebab-slug>.md`, `kind ∈ {principle, framework, case-study, heuristic, claim}`.
41	
42	```yaml
43	---
44	type: library-entry
45	kind: principle
46	domain: <domain-slug>
47	book: <book-slug>
48	chapter: "N"            # or section label; "" if highlights with no location
49	topic: <2-5 word topic>
50	category: [tag, tag]
51	confidence: proven      # proven | supported | untested | contested
52	ingest-tier: full-text  # full-text | highlights | framework-only
53	created: <YYYY-MM-DD>
54	---
55	
56	# <Human title of the idea>
57	
58	**What it is** — one tight paragraph.
59	**Why it works** — mechanism, not restatement.
60	**When to apply** — concrete triggers.
61	**When NOT to apply** — scope limits. (MANDATORY — never omit.)
62	**Example** — one concrete instance.
63	```
64	
65	**Confidence is bounded by tier:** full-text ≤ proven; highlights ≤ supported;
66	framework-only ≤ untested. Set `contested` by hand when sources conflict.
67	
68	## Phase 1 — Intake
69	
70	1. Identify: book title, author, source type (PDF/EPUB | Kindle highlights | physical), target domain.
71	2. Compute `<book-slug>` = `kebab(title)--kebab(lastname)` (e.g. `supertraining--verkhoshansky`).
72	3. If the domain folder/`_domain.md` doesn't exist, create them (mirror the S&C `_domain.md` format).
73	4. Build `_book.md` chapter map:
74	   - EPUB/PDF: run the extractor with `--list` / `--probe` to get the chapter or page structure.
75	   - Physical: ask the user for the chapter list, or assemble from a verified public listing.
76	   Write `_book.md` (template below) with every chapter `status: pending`.
77	
78	`_book.md` template:
79	```markdown
80	---
81	type: book-index
82	book: <book-slug>
83	title: <full title>
84	author: <author>
85	domain: <domain-slug>
86	ingest-tier: full-text | highlights | framework-only
87	source: "<file path or 'physical' or 'kindle-highlights'>"
88	created: <YYYY-MM-DD>
89	---
90	
91	# <title> — ingest map
92	
93	| # | Chapter | Status | Entries |
94	|---|---------|--------|---------|
95	| 0 | <title> | pending | 0 |
96	```
97	
98	## Phase 2 — Extract (by tier)
99	
100	**Full-text (PDF/EPUB):**
101	- First run `extract_pdf.py --probe`. If `scanned: true`, STOP the full-text path:
102	  tell the user the PDF is image-only, and fall back to framework-only tier (set
103	  `ingest-tier: framework-only`, cap confidence at untested). Never emit full-text-
104	  confidence entries from a scanned file.
105	- Work **one chapter at a time** (EPUB `--chapter N`; PDF `--pages A-B`, where A and B are
106	  0-based PDF indexes and the range is inclusive: `--pages 12-20` returns 9 pages). Each page
107	  comes back with `page` (0-based index) and `viewer_page` (what a PDF viewer shows, index + 1).
108	  Cite pages one way throughout a book and state the convention in `_book.md`. For each:
109	  extract candidate ideas → atomize per the schema → write entry notes.
110	- **After each chapter**, update that row in `_book.md` to `status: done` with the
111	  entry count. This is the resume checkpoint — never batch this update.
112	
113	**Kindle highlights:**
114	- Parse `My Clippings.txt` or the highlights export in the sandbox. Cluster highlights
115	  by theme; write one entry per theme. `ingest-tier: highlights`, confidence ≤ supported.
116	- Attribute `chapter` from the highlight's location metadata when present, else "".
117	
118	**Framework-only (physical / scanned):**
119	- Briefly interview the user for their takeaways. Supplement with *verified* public
120	  chapter summaries. Write 5–15 framework-level entries. `ingest-tier: framework-only`,
121	  confidence ≤ untested.
122	
123	## Phase 3 — Quality gate (run before writing each batch)
124	
125	- One idea per note. If an extracted point is compound, split it.
126	- "When NOT to apply" present and non-trivial.
127	- **Dedup + converge:** before writing, `memsearch search` the library for the same
128	  concept. If an existing entry (any book) covers it, DON'T duplicate — instead add a
129	  `[[wikilink]]` + one line to both notes recording the agreement, and only add a new
130	  note if it contributes a genuinely new angle.
131	- Never overwrite an existing file; on slug collision append `-2`.
132	
133	## Phase 4 — Close-out
134	
135	1. Set all done rows in `_book.md`; if partial, leave pending rows for next session.
136	2. Add the book to `_domain.md`'s `books:` list and the "Books in this domain" section.
137	3. Add the book-slug to the advisor persona's `books:` list (`advisors/<domain>.md`)
138	   if an advisor exists.
139	4. Run `memsearch index "<vault_library>"` using the selected platform config
140	   so entries are searchable immediately (don't wait for the SessionEnd hook).
141	5. Commit the vault using `vault_root` from the selected platform config: `git -C "<vault_root>" add Knowledge/library && git commit -m "ingest(<book-slug>): <N> entries, ch X-Y"`.
142	6. Report: entries by kind and confidence, links created, chapters remaining.
143	
144	## Rules
145	- Raw book text stays in the sandbox; only atomized entries enter context/the vault.
146	- Resumable by design: `_book.md` is the source of truth for "where am I".
147	- A 300-page book is a multi-session job — stop at a chapter boundary, never mid-chapter.
148	=================== research-in-5
149	---
150	name: research-in-5
151	description: "Build a \"Research in 5\" weekly paper review for Baylor Athletics staff: a 5-slide deck (dark and light), a Teams post, and a staff email from one paper. Use when the user says \"/research-in-5\", \"research in 5 on this paper\", \"weekly research review\", \"review this paper for the staff\", \"make the slides for this paper\", hands over a paper (PDF, DOI, URL, Zotero item), or wants a review rebuilt or versioned (#001, v2). Do not use for a sport-science question (use sports-science-research-grounding), a deck with no single paper (use five-slides-generator), or a plain Zotero search."
152	---
153	
154	# Research in 5
155	
156	The procedure, content rules, and build tooling live in the project repo, not here.
157	This skill gets you into the repo and carries the lessons that are easy to relearn
158	the hard way.
159	
160	## Start
161	
162	1. Project root: `~/Desktop/DEV/Weekly_Research_Review` (Windows) or
163	   `~/DEV/Weekly_Research_Review` (Mac). Missing on this machine:
164	   `gh repo clone erash11/Weekly_Research_Review` into DEV.
165	2. `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, and
166	   `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`. Follow WORKFLOW.md step by step; it owns the process.
167	3. Background session: work in a worktree of that repo, open a PR, merge only when
168	   Eric says so.
169	
170	Build and QA: `pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug -NoDrive`, read every
171	`dark-slideN.png` and `light-slideN.png`, then publish without `-NoDrive`.
172	Deliverables land in `07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5/NNN_slug/` on the Google Drive
173	primary storage drive.
174	
175	## Gotchas
176	
177	- **Check Zotero for the full text before settling for an abstract.** A new item's PDF may not be indexed yet: run `sync_zotero_library` with `include_fulltext: true`, then `get_paper` and look at `attachments`. #001 was first built from the abstract while the PDF sat in Zotero.
178	- **Article-in-press papers often have no public PDF.** Springer's PDF URL 404s even in Chrome. Ask Eric for the PDF or check Zotero; set `paper.full_text: false` only as a last resort and say so in the post.
179	- **Every number comes from the paper's tables, with a page, as reported.** Write `notes.md` first. Plot and tabulate exact values; never display a computed difference. Flag contradictions inside the paper (a conclusion stronger than its own limitations, a mislabeled table) in notes.md.
180	- **Slides carry one idea each; detail goes to the post.** Slide-facing fields have tight limits that build.js enforces (question 90, fact 26, summary 110, role line 70, takeaway 60, bottom line 55). Write those short first. `did.bullets`, `results.bullets`, extra limitations, and the discussion question are post-only.
181	- **Department names:** Athletic Performance (not strength and conditioning), Athletic Medicine (not sports medicine), Applied Performance (not sport science). build.js rejects others.
182	- **Baylor Bears Font has only A to Z, 0 to 9, space and `. : ! - #`.** It sets display text only; `headline` must fit that set. Section titles are caps statements because there is no `?`. Agency FB sets everything people read and has no `→`.
183	- **"Calibri" in the PDF font list is expected.** PowerPoint cannot embed Bears (OpenType-CFF) and draws it as outlines with a Calibri-tagged text layer. Only `Agency FB embedded: False` is a real failure. Both fonts must be installed before building on a new machine (`DEV/Baylor_Fonts`).
184	- **Run the humanizer skill on the audience copy before the final build.** Keep facts, pages, and limits; cut rule-of-three lists, "not X, but Y" lines, and stacked rhetorical questions.
185	- **Revisions get a new `version`** (outputs `_vN`) so the files Eric may already have shared stay on Drive. Only overwrite in place for a same-day correction, and say so.
186	- **The deck is checked against the paper before it can publish.** Step 5 runs `pwsh tools/verify.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug`; `publish.ps1` runs it again and refuses to copy anything to Drive on a real finding. Three outcomes: **VERIFY FAIL** means a claim is fabricated, contradicted, unsupported, or on the wrong page, so fix review.json and rebuild. **VERIFY PASS** may still name claims needing a human read - those are the `[REVIEW]` lines, where the model was not confident enough to decide, and you read them against notes.md. **VERIFY DEGRADED** means the check could not run at all (it needs the `TypeSafe_Sandbox` clone, its venv, and `~/.claude/typesafe.env`); it does not block, but report it like a DEGRADED image QA - the deck went out unchecked. `-SkipVerify` bypasses the gate; only use it after checking by hand, and say so.

190	- **Propose a rule when one was missing.** If a problem got past build.js and verify.ps1 (caught in the PNG read, the humanizer pass, or by Eric), end the run by proposing one new gotcha line here or one new check in `CONTENT_SPEC.md`, with the reason. Add it only on Eric's yes.
